column4: The start-up's second step (_start calls it): fills the stack from 0x8C00C000 to 0x8C00F000 and the RAM from 0x8C1EA4F8 to 0x8C1EA520 with the word SEGA (0x41474553), sets the program's sections up (startupSections) and runs gameMain. It loops for ever if gameMain returns.

Sets the program's sections up: clears the RAM from 0x8C124C40 to 0x8C1EA4F8 and from 0x8C10AF34 to 0x8C124C40, and copies the two initialized data ranges from the image, which are empty in this program.
Sets the function that njEORCallback calls at the end of each render.
Kamui's end-of-render callback. Calls the function set with njSetEORCallback if one is set.
Kamui's end-of-vertex callback. Calls the function set with njSetEOVCallback if one is set.
Ninja's njHSyncCallback: njInitSystem passes it to kmSetHSyncCallback. Its code has the same shape as njEORCallback's.
Kamui's PAL extension callback. Writes Ninja's PAL height ratio to offset 4 of the structure it gets.
Initializes the Kamui device with kmInitDevice and Ninja's globals with njInitGlobal, then clears two Ninja state words.
Sets up the display mode, the frame buffer and Ninja's Kamui callbacks. The game calls it with the display mode, the frame buffer mode and the vsync count.

Ninja's njSetWaitVsyncCount, by its place in the SDK object njSystem_, whose other functions match here.
Ninja's njCnkEasyMultiDrawMotionLink: passes njCnkEasyMultiDrawModel to njDrawMotionLink, as the SDK object njCnkMotionLinkEM_ does.
Ninja's njCnkEasyDrawMotionLink: passes njCnkEasyDrawModel to njDrawMotionLink, as the SDK object njCnkMotionLinkE_ does.
Ninja's njCnkSimpleMultiDrawMotionLink: passes njCnkSimpleMultiDrawModel to njDrawMotionLink, as the SDK object njCnkMotionLinkSM_ does.
Ninja's njCnkSimpleDrawMotionLink: passes njCnkSimpleDrawModel to njDrawMotionLink, as the SDK object njCnkMotionLinkS_ does.

Ninja's njCameraMotion (camera, motion, frame), by its place in the SDK object njMotionCamera_. endingBgDraw calls it.

Ninja's njCnkSetEasyLightIntensity, by its place in the SDK object njCnkModelE_ (offsets 0, 14 and 28).
Ninja's njCnkSetEasyLightColor, by its place in the SDK object njCnkModelE_ (offsets 0, 14 and 28).
Walks the polygon list of a chunk model with Easy lighting and draws its strips with njCnkEasyPolygon, njCnkEasyTexture and their clip and bump variants.
Ninja's njCnkEasyDrawModel, by its place in the SDK object njCnkModelE_. njCnkEasyDrawMotionLink passes it.

Ninja's njCnkSimpleDrawObject: passes njCnkSimpleDrawModel to njCnkTransformObject, as njCnkEasyDrawObject does for the Easy model.

Ninja's njCnkSetSimpleMultiLightMatrices, from the SDK object njCnkSimpleMultiLight_, whose functions lie here in order. The Easy object has the same code: the njCnkSimpleMulti neighbours decide.
Returns the word at offset 0x24 of the DMA handle it gets.
Writes one character to the debug serial port of the address checker, in SCIF or SCI mode. It waits until the transmitter is free, writes the character and waits until it is sent.
Shinobi's syRtcGetDate, by its place in the SDK object sg_syRtc, whose other functions match here.
Shinobi's syRtcCountToDate, by its place in the SDK object sg_syRtc, whose other functions match here.
Shinobi's syRtcGetAndCheckCount, by its place in the SDK object sg_syRtc, whose other functions match here.
Shinobi's syRtcGetCountForce, by its place in the SDK object sg_syRtc, whose other functions match here.
Shinobi's syRtcAicaGetCount, by its place in the SDK object sg_syRtc, 0x20 later than in the SDK's copy, with the same size.
Shinobi's syRtcMakeDayOfWeek, by its place in the SDK object sg_syRtc, 0x20 later than in the SDK's copy, with the same size.
Returns the age of the moon in days (0 to 29) for a date. It takes the seconds since a reference new moon modulo 2551423 seconds, about one synodic month, and divides them by 86400.
Appends one word to the RTC debug log when logging is on (flag 8) and the log buffer has room.

Clears the G2 time-out bit (bit 27) of the error interrupt status register 0xA05F6908 with interrupts masked. It writes the read value back with bit 27 set, so it also clears every other pending error bit.
Clears the G2 time-out bit and reads one word from the given G2 address. Returns 1 when the read causes no G2 time-out and the word is the signature GAPS (0x53504147), else 0.
Writes 0 to the register at offset 0x14 of the device at the given G2 address with interrupts masked. Returns true when the G2 write succeeds.

Writes 0x5A00A500, with bits 8 to 15 of the device address put into bits 16 to 23, to the register at offset 0x18 of the device at that G2 address with interrupts masked. Returns true when the G2 write succeeds.
The sound library's sdBankDownloadEx, by its place in the SDK object sd_bank_download_ex_.
Downloads an MLT sound file to sound memory with sdMltDownloadEx and reports an error to sdSysErrTrap.
Starts the download of an MLT sound file to sound memory. Allocates the sound memory blocks and sets sdMltDownloadExCallback as the transfer callback.
Memory block callback of sdMltDownloadEx. Accounts for each finished transfer, starts the next one and calls sdMltDownloadExFinish after the last.
The sound library's sdMidiSetPan: the same bytes as the SDK object sd_midi_set_pan_. The midi and shot versions are identical, and the neighbours decide.
Sets the release mode (0 or 1) of a MIDI handle. Reports an error to sdSysErrTrap when the library is not initialized, the handle is null or the mode is invalid.
The sound library's sdMidiSetVol: the same bytes as the SDK object sd_midi_set_vol_. The midi and shot versions are identical, and the neighbours decide. The port's NO MUSIC wraps it.
The sound library's sdShotSetPan: the same bytes as the SDK object sd_shot_set_pan_. The midi and shot versions are identical, and the neighbours decide.
Sets the release mode (0 or 1) of a one-shot handle. Reports an error to sdSysErrTrap when the library is not initialized, the handle is null or the mode is invalid.
The sound library's sdShotSetVol: the same bytes as the SDK object sd_shot_set_vol_. The midi and shot versions are identical, and the neighbours decide.
Initializes the sound library. Sets up the work area with sdSysWrkInit and adds sdSysVsyncServer to the vsync interrupt chain with interrupts masked.
Sets up the sound library's work area at sdgWrkPtr. Initializes the memory blocks, the block queue, the host command buffers and the module references.

Sets the system up, as the SDK's sbInitSystem does but without Ninja: syHwInit, the heap from the program's end to 0x8D000000 (syMallocInit), systemStartHook, the fibers (syFbrInitEx), the controllers (pdInitPeripheral), syCallbackInit, the GD-ROM file system for 8 files and 0x400 directory entries (gdFsInit2), syFsInit and the clock (syRtcInit). gameMain calls it first.
Shuts the system down in the opposite order of systemInit, with the C++ static destructors (systemExitHook) before syMallocFinish. gameMain calls it at its end.
Calls startupEmpty, which does nothing. systemInit calls it after syMallocInit.
Runs the C++ static destructors (staticDestructorsRun). systemExit calls it before syMallocFinish.
Starts the sound library (FUN_8c055f7c), loads the sound driver MANATEE.DRV (fileLoad), passes it to sdDrvInit in a memory block and frees the file. gameMain calls it before gameInit.

Stops all sound, clears the effect programs, closes every MIDI, stream and one-shot player, destroys the memory blocks and finishes the sound library (sdSysFinish). gameMain calls it when its loop ends.
Shinobi's buGetDiskFree, by its place in the SDK object vmsapi_.
Shinobi's buIsExistFile, by its place in the SDK object vmsapi_.

Fills the BUS_DISKINFO of a memory card drive: the 32-byte volume data, the block counts, the free blocks from vmsfs_diskfree, the icon number and the format time. Returns 0, or a negative error code when the drive is not ready, not mounted or not formatted.

Counts the free blocks (FAT entry 0xFFFC) of a memory card drive. With mode 1 it counts the free blocks in a row from block 0, which an executable file needs, otherwise all free user blocks. Returns the count or a negative error code.

Opens an existing file on a memory card drive by name. It finds the directory entry, takes a free file handle, sets its first block and size and stores the handle in the third argument. Returns 0 or a negative error code.

Creates the executable (game) file on a memory card drive. It fails when the name exists, when another executable file exists or when block 0 is not free, otherwise it takes a directory entry and a file handle and returns the handle in the fourth argument.
Returns the size in blocks of the named file on a memory card drive, read from its directory entry, or a negative error code.
Finds the executable (game) file on a memory card drive and copies its 12-character name, zero terminated, to the second argument. Returns 0 or a negative error code.

Creates a data file on a memory card drive and writes it block by block with the bank locked, then reads every block back and compares it with the source. Returns 0, the error of a failed step, or -0xF0 when a block differs.

Creates the executable file on a memory card drive and writes it block by block with the bank locked, then reads every block back and compares it with the source. Returns 0, the error of a failed step, or -0xF0 when a block differs.

Sets the current block of an open file to its first block, then follows the FAT chain forward by the given number of blocks and counts down the blocks left. Returns the blocks left, or 0xFFFF0000 when the end of the chain and the block count disagree.

Writes one block from the buffer over the current block of an open file in place and moves to the next block of its FAT chain. Returns the blocks left, 0 at the end of the file, or a negative error code.
The C library's printf, for a number's digits: rounds the digits at a position, carrying into the ones before it.

The C++ runtime at the program's end (gameMain's shutdown calls it): takes each entry of the list at 0x8C15C48C (next, destructor, object) from its head and calls the destructor with the object and -1. Nothing else in the program refers to the list's head.
Does nothing. The system's start-up calls it through systemStartHook after syMallocInit.

The C++ runtime for an array under construction, reached only through exception tables. Takes a record (start, element size, element count, destructor, elements built): when fewer elements were built than the count and the destructor is not 0, calls the destructor with -1 on each built element, from the last. Frees the record itself when the second argument is above 0.
Signed 32-bit division, from another runtime library than the SDK-named __divls. A test of the C++ gave -7 / 2 = -3.
Unsigned 32-bit division, from another runtime library than the SDK-named __divlu. A test of the C++ gave 0xFFFFFFF9 / 2 = 0x7FFFFFFC.
Signed 32-bit remainder, from another runtime library than the SDK-named __modls. A test of the C++ gave -7 % 2 = -1.
Unsigned 32-bit remainder, from another runtime library than the SDK-named __modlu. chainBonus picks a random sound with it.
Sets the work buffer for loading textures from the disc and its size in bytes, which it rounds down to whole sectors of 2,048 bytes. gameMain calls it.
The work buffer for loading textures and its size (textureBufferSet).
Reads a palette file from the disc into the texture buffer and gives it to Ninja as palette data. Returns -1 on an error.

Loads one texture of a texture list at once by its attributes (attr & 0x5C000000): 0 from its file on the disc, 0x40000000 from PVR data in memory, other values only enter or link it in Ninja's texture management without loading data. Returns 1 when done and -1 on an error.
Loads each texture of a texture list at once (textureLoad) and stops at the first that fails. Returns 1 when all are loaded, and -1 on an error or for a list without textures.
Starts reading a PVM archive in memory: sets its start and the read position.
Returns the read position in a PVM archive and moves it on by a size.
Moves the read position in a PVM archive: from the start with 0, from where it is with 1.
Copies 2 bytes, one at a time, so that neither address needs alignment.
Copies 4 bytes, one at a time, so that neither address needs alignment.

Reads a PVM archive's entries into a texture list: each entry's number into the low 16 bits of attr, its name into filename when the header has flag 1, and, when the header has flag 8 and attr has neither 0x800000 nor 0x1000000, its global index into texaddr with attr 0x800000.
The size of each entry in a PVM archive's header, from the header's flags.
Moves through a PVM archive's chunks to the next texture (PVRT), and gives Ninja the palettes (PVPL) on the way.
Fills a texture list from a PVM archive in memory (magic PVMH) and loads its textures. Returns -1 on an error.
Loads a texture list's textures in steps, one texture after the other (textureLoadStep). Returns 0 while it works, 1 when all are loaded and -1 on an error.

Loads one texture of a list in steps, from its file on the disc or from memory: runs the step function of the current state from the table at 0x8C0CF7F8 until a step clears the flag at 0x8C0CF7E4, which it does when it waits, ends or fails. Returns 0 while it works, 1 when done and -1 on an error.

Texture load step 1: ends with 1 when njCheckAttrGlobalIndex returns 1 (Ninja holds the texture already) and fails with -1 when it returns -1. Else on to step 2 for a texture in a file, or 6 for one in memory (attr 0x40000000).
Texture load step 2: opens the texture's file for reading into the texture buffer.
Texture load step 3: asks the disc for the next sectors of the texture's file.
Texture load step 4: waits for the disc's read.
Texture load step 5: reads a texture's PVR header from its file's data.
Texture load step 6: reads the PVR header of a texture in memory.
Texture load step 7: enters the texture into Ninja's texture management.
Texture load step 8: loads a part of the texture into texture memory.
Texture load step 9: waits for the texture's DMA, then reads the next part or ends.

Stops a texture load of textureLoadStep: sets its state and the list's texture index to 0. Only when the load waits for a DMA (step 9) does it stop the disc read and close the file, and then returns -1 when gdFsStopRd fails. Else returns 1.
Reads a whole file from the disc into a buffer, if it fits. Returns -1 on an error.
Swaps the byte order of a 32-bit word.
Stops the disc read that fileReadStart began, closes the file and frees its buffer.
Loads one file of a bank's list: in steps from a task (fileReadStart, fileReadPoll, fileReadEnd), or at once (fileLoad).

Goes on through a bank's list from where it stopped, up to the end mark (type 5): models (modelFileLoad, types 0 and 1), files with texture names (bankFileLoad and njSetTextureName, types 2 and 3) and a directory (fileSetDir, type 4). Then loads the bank's texture list. Returns 1 while a load waits or another bank loads, 0 when the bank is loaded and -1 on an error.
The task that loads a bank over frames (bankLoadStep). Ends when the bank is loaded, and shows the disc error screen on an error.

Stops the disc loads: the file read of fileReadStart and, while a bank's textures load in steps, the texture load, after which it mounts the disc again (gdFsReMount). Clears the lock that lets one bank load at a time. gameRelease and gameEnterScene call it.

Loads a graphics bank's list of files under a name. Shows the disc error screen while the bank still loads, returns at once when the loaded bank has that name already, and frees a loaded bank of another name (bankFree). Then loads at once (mode 0) or in a bankLoadTask over frames.
Loads a bank's files at once (bankLoadFiles with mode 0).
Loads a bank's files at once (bankLoadFiles with mode 0) and keeps a function in the bank that bankLoadStep calls after each entry of the list, when it is not 0. Its one caller passes 0.
Loads a bank's files in a task over frames (bankLoadFiles with mode 1).
Loads a bank's files with a mode: 0 at once, else in a task over frames (bankLoadFiles).
Returns a bank's load state: -1 when it is empty (bankClear), 1 when bankLoadFiles has set it up, 2 while bankLoadStep loads it and 0 when it is loaded.
Frees what a bank holds, its models, motions and textures, and clears it (bankClear).
Sets the game's data up at gameInit: clears the fade, gives Ninja the 4 palette files, loads bank 0 (SYSDAT), sets fogFadeApply as a callback of each frame and resets the fog.
Turns the fog and the fade of fogFadeApply off, sets the fog mode, and sets Ninja's near and far clip.
Splits four ARGB colors into their 16 channels, for the fade's mixing.
Mixes one ARGB color from a start and a target set of four channels (colorsSplit) by a fraction f: each channel is start * (1 - f) + target * f, cut to an integer.
The task of fadeTo: waits until no other fade runs, then moves the fade's four corners from their colors to the target colors over its frames.
Marks every fade task (fadeTask) of list 0 for removal and clears the flag of a running fade, unless a fade is held (fadeHold, which gameOverCheck sets).
Clears the fade's two flags: the one that fadeTask sets while it fades and the hold that stops fadeTo and fadeStop. Fade tasks that exist go on.
Finds the first textured strip chunk (type 0x41) of a chunk model and returns its strip count and data in a new block, for uvStripsScroll.
Moves the texture coordinates of each vertex of a model's strips (uvStripsFind) by du and dv, which scrolls the texture over the model.
Counts a model's objects and those of its children, for modelNodeTreeCreate.
Fills a tree of draw nodes, one for each object of a model, with the links to each node's first child and next sibling.

Makes a tree of draw nodes for a model of a bank (id: the bank in the high 16 bits, the model in the low 16 bits), one node for each object, or returns 0 when the allocation fails. The callers set some nodes' functions, which turn or scale a part, take its matrix, file its hit records or draw another model there.

Draws a model through its node tree. For each object it moves, turns and scales the matrix by the object's values, calls the node's function with the caller's value, and draws the object's model with the node's draw function or the default one, unless the object has no model or its flag 8 is set. Then it draws the children in the object's matrix and goes on with the siblings.

Sets a model of a bank up (modelSetup) and draws it through a node tree (modelNodeTreeCreate, nodeTreeDraw), with the default draw function that flags & 0xf picks from the table at 0x8C0CFA90. Returns 0x3f and draws nothing when modelSetup leaves the model out, else 0.
A sprite vertex builder of the vertical screen, for the kinds without a scale (spriteDraw's flag bits 1 to 3): turns the corners by the sprite's angle and a quarter turn about the screen's centre.
A sprite vertex builder of the vertical screen, for the kinds with a scale: scales the corners, then turns them by the sprite's angle and a quarter turn about the screen's centre.

The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 0 (spriteDraw's flag bits 1 to 3): places the corners at the position, turned by the angle when it is not 0, and fits them to the screen's aspect.

The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 2 (spriteDraw's flag bits 1 to 3): places the corners at the position, turned by the angle when it is not 0, and scales the corners, not the position, by the screen's aspect.

The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 4 (spriteDraw's flag bits 1 to 3): places the corners at the position, turned by the angle when it is not 0, and fits the position, not the corners, to the screen's aspect about the screen's centre.
The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 6 (spriteDraw's flag bits 1 to 3): places the corners at the position, turned by the angle when it is not 0.
The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 1: as spriteCorners0, with the sprite's x and y scale.
The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 3: as spriteCorners2, with the sprite's x and y scale.
The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 5: as spriteCorners4, with the sprite's x and y scale.
The sprite vertex builder of the horizontal screen for kind 7: as spriteCorners6, with the sprite's x and y scale.

Gives textDraw two vectors of 16 on a vertical screen, turned by the text's angle and a quarter turn: the advance of a full-width character and the side of a character's quad from its top to its bottom.
Gives textDraw two vectors of 16 on a horizontal screen, turned by the text's angle: the advance of a full-width character and the side of a character's quad from its top to its bottom.
As textStepsVertical, for a text with a scale.
As textSteps, for a text with a scale.

Copies the boot ROM font's 24-dot glyph (72 bytes) of a Shift-JIS character for a text line's texture and returns 0. When the font's semaphore is taken (syBtFntChkSmph) it copies nothing and returns -1. The port replaces it (port/src/bios.cpp): without a ROM image, macOS's Hiragino draws the glyph.

Copies a 24-dot glyph into a text line's texture at x and y in one color, each set dot also onto the dot right of it, the dot below it and the dot below and right of it, inside the 24-dot cell. The port wraps it (port/src/text.cpp).
Makes a texture of a line of Shift-JIS text with the ROM font's glyphs, for the menus' help, CONFIG and the messages. The port wraps it for ENGLISH TEXT (port/src/text.cpp).
Frees a text line's texture (textLineTexture).
Draws a text line's texture as a sprite, with the sprite vertex builder and the blending that its flags pick.

Turns the points of a 2D polygon by a quarter turn about the screen's centre and fits them to Ninja's aspect. The draw functions call it on a horizontal screen and draw the points unturned on a vertical one.

Gives a screen position for the screen's orientation: mode 0 takes x and y from the top left, mode 1 from the screen's centre (320, 240). A horizontal screen keeps the position, a vertical one turns it by a quarter (640 - y, x for mode 0). Other modes write nothing.
Turns off what fogFadeApply applies: Ninja's fog, or its fade, by the mode.
Makes the fog's table from a near and a far depth (njGenerateFogTable3).
Sets the fog's color from red, green and blue.
A callback of each frame (gameDataInit): while it is on, applies the fog table, or Ninja's fade at its level, by the mode.
Sets the level of Ninja's fade that fogFadeApply applies in the fade mode.
Draws a black polygon with an alpha over the whole screen.

Turns the lit lights of Ninja's multi-light models into the view through a unit matrix, turned by a quarter (njRotateZ by -0x4000) on a vertical screen. Bit 0 does it for the Easy models' lights and bit 1 for the Simple models'.
Sets the count of the frame's extra lights (lightAdd) to 0. gameTaskFrame calls it before it runs the task lists, except while pauseState is 1.
Adds one of up to 4 extra point lights for this frame, as light 3 to 6 of the Easy and the Simple multi-light models, with a position, a color and two ranges. With 4 lights added it does nothing.
Sets the light values to a mix of two light settings by a fraction.
The task of lightsFadeTo: mixes the lights from the start setting to the target one over its frames (lightsMix), then ends.
Makes the task that mixes the lights from one setting to another over a number of frames (lightsFadeTask).
Moves the lights from their current setting to another over a number of frames. The stages change their light with it.
Stops every sound and closes the sound library's 8 sequence players and 20 one-shot players, at gameRelease.
Frees a slot of soundBankLists.
The task of sequencePlay's mode 1: waits until a slot of the sound's range is free, then starts the sequence and ends.
Sets up sequenceWaitTask's data: the sound id and the range of slots that its bank list's entry gives.
Sets the speed of the sequence in a slot (sdMidiSeqSetSpeed).
Stops the sequence in a slot and frees the slot, when the slot is in use and soundOff is not set.
Sets the volume of the sequence in a slot over a time (the sound library's MIDI volume, which the port's NO MUSIC wraps).
Sets the pan of the sequence in a slot from a position (soundPan), when it changed.

Starts a sequence by its sound id unless soundOff is set: at once with mode 0, or with mode 1 as soon as one of its slots is free (sequenceWaitTask). Returns the slot with mode 0, else -1. The mode select and the chapters start their music with it.
Stops every one-shot sound and frees their slots.
Sets the pan and the volume of the one-shot sound in a slot from a position, when the pan changed and soundOff is not set.
Stops the one-shot sound in a slot and frees the slot, when the slot is in use and soundOff is not set.
The task of effectFadeOut: counts its frames down, then stops the sound and ends.
Unless soundOff is set, fades the one-shot sound in a slot out over a number of frames, then stops it (effectFadeOutTask).
Stops every sequence and one-shot sound (soundStopSequences, effectsStopAll) and sets the speed of slot 0's sequence player to 0.
The slot when it still plays the sequence with this sound id, else -1.
Returns the slot when it still plays the one-shot sound with this sound id, and -1 when the slot is free or plays another sound. For a slot outside 0 to 19 it returns no defined value.
Clears the image of a port's VMU screen.
Returns the low 16 bits in reverse order. vmuImageSet and vmuChainShow turn a VMU image round with it, 16 pixels of a row at a time.

Copies a 48 by 32 pixel image into VMU screen 0 or 1, turned round when pdLcdGetDirection returns nonzero. It asks pdLcdGetDirection about port 1 for screen 0 but about port 0 for screen 1, whose VMU is at port 7.
Shows a player's chain on the VMU's screen: its digits over an image.
Clears both VMU screens' images (vmuImageClear) and states, at gameInit.
Runs both VMU screens (vmuScreenUpdate): at each frame in gameFrame, and in gameEnterScene while an autosave writes and for 30 frames after it succeeds.
The two Ninja angles of a direction: the turn about y from atan2(-x, -z), and the pitch from y over the length in x and z.
The two Ninja angles of the direction from one point to another (vectorAngles).
Returns a new block with the intervals between a path's distances at consecutive points, or 0 without memory. pathCreate passes it to pathSlopes and pathCurves.
The slope of a path's value between each two points: its change over the interval, for the straight segments.
Solves a natural cubic spline through one value of a path's points, for the curved segments: the second derivatives divided by 6, with 0 at both ends. Returns -1 when it has no memory, else 0.
The callback that cardInit gives buInit. It does nothing.
Starts the memory card library (buInit with capacity 0xF and drives 1), at gameInit.

Sets a player's joined mark (the byte at 0x8C15C518 plus the player, which playerJoin sets to 1) back to 0xFF when it is set. The end paths of a game call it (continueEnd, pauseQuit, pauseRestart, stageCmdEnd).
Draws AUTO SAVE... and renders, while a scene change saves to the card.

Draws AUTO SAVE...FAILED and three lines of Japanese text that say the autosave failed and stops from now on, renders, and waits 5 vertical blanks. gameEnterScene calls it after a failed autosave and then waits 720 more.

Computes a player's buttons with repeat for the name entry: each of 11 buttons fires when it goes down and, after 15 frames held, every second frame. The result goes to the player's word at 0x8C1D13D4.
Runs the button repeat for both players (padRepeatUpdate). nameEntryInput calls it each time it runs.
Clears both players' button repeat counters and stores its argument in the byte at 0x8C1D1390. nameEntryTask calls it with 0 when a name entry starts.

The task of easeWord. With a lock, it first waits until the lock is 0 and takes it. Then it moves the word one frame along the curve each frame, and at the end it sets the word to the value, frees the lock unless flag 0x80 leaves that to easeWordEnd, and ends.
Frees the lock at the removal of easeWord's task.
Frees the lock at the removal of easeFloat's task.

Outside the attract mode, draws CREDIT(S) and the count, or FREE PLAY, at the screen's edge in the mode select and while the game is paused outside the tutorial, and fades it out over 30 frames after. Holding X and Y in the pause hides it.
In the attract mode (gameDemo) outside the title, Start on either pad stops every sound and requests the title, when no scene request is pending. Returns 1 then, else 0.
The draw of a vibration's task: ends the task while the game is paused.
Clears the vibration units' requests, at gameInit.
Raises chapterReached for the difficulty to the current chapter.
At the start of chapters 2 to 5: raises chapterReached when the players got there without a continue (both players in a two-player game), unless the game is a practice or a demo.
Keeps playersInGame and gamePrototype, clears both and starts player 1 (playerStart). stageStart calls it in scene 11, and playersRestore undoes it.

Gives back playersInGame and gamePrototype that playersKeep kept, applies the options and starts the players again. In the prototype mode each ship gets 500 energy minus 200 for each step of difficulty.
Clears a player's chain and its current set, and tells the VMU's screen (event 0).
The task of scrollStopAt: once scrollPosition reaches the braking point that scrollStopAt computed, sets scrollTarget to 0 and scrollStep to the deceleration, and ends.
Lets either player join with Start (playerJoinCheck). modeSelectUpdate calls it at the end of each run.
Plays the sound of the continue's count for continueTimer (soundPlay): sound 0x37 at 0 down to 0x2e at 9.

The draw of the stage's task. In the tutorial outside the attract demo, Start or B leaves for sceneNext, in a trial game only Start of a player who was in the game. Else, outside the attract demo, it counts continueTimer down during a continue, each count at most 128 frames with its sound (continueCountSound), shows CONTINUE while both ships are out, and lets a player who is out join with Start and a credit (playerJoinCheck), which unlocks the player's pause and sets pauseEnd while pausePlayer is 0.
Frees the camera's path at the removal of the stage's task.
Replaces a name before it enters the rankings: a blank name, AAA and three names of X become TRE, the default entries' name, and a rude word becomes H !.
Ends a player's name entry: filters the name (nameEntryFilter) and puts the scores into the rankings (rankingAdd).

Returns the letter of a name entry's cursor position: A to Z for 0x41 to 0x5a, the digits 0 to 9 for 0x5b to 0x64, the signs ! ? @ # $ % & for 0x65 to 0x6b, and a space for the keys SP, BS and ED (0x6c to 0x6e) and any other value.
Returns the name entry's cursor position of a letter, nameEntryChar backwards for A to Z, the digits and ! ? @. Any other letter, also # $ % & and the space, gives 0x6c, the SP key.
Draws the name entry's SP key, which enters a space, as two letters.
Draws the name entry's BS key, which takes the last letter back, as two letters.
Draws the name entry's ED key, which ends the entry, as two letters.
Takes the name entry's last letter back, with B or the BS key.
Enters the name entry's letter at the cursor, or after the third letter ends the entry (nameEntryFinish).
Fills the name from the cursor's position with spaces and ends the entry (nameEntryConfirm). nameEntryInput calls it for the ED key, and nameEntryTask when the entry's 1860 frames run out.

A player's input in the name entry each frame: left and right move the cursor with repeat, or at the fourth position switch between BS and ED. A or C presses the key at the cursor, which enters a letter or a space, takes a letter back (BS) or ends the entry (ED), and B takes a letter back.

Keeps a player's scores for the ranking lists (chapterScores): the total in entry 0, and in the chapter's entry (sceneCurrent - 5) the total minus the earlier chapters' entries and the chapter's longest chain (chainMax). resultsStep calls it for both players and playerOut when a player loses the last ship.

Fills the third block of chapterScores, for the two-player lists, entry by entry from both players' blocks: the score as their sum (scoreTotal) and the chain as the sum of their chains. First it sets each player's entry 0 to the player's score with a chain of 0.
Frees one of the pause menu's two textures of its help line.
Makes the texture of a new help line for the pause menu in its other buffer, unless the line is shown already.
Draws the pause menu's help line on its panel.
Frees both textures of the pause menu's help line, also at the removal of its task.
Sets the pause menu back to its first item and frees its help line.

Lets the player who paused end the pause with Start, once the Start that paused was let go: it clears the player's bit in pausePlayer, and pauseMenuDraw then ends the pause. It does nothing after Restart or Quit was chosen.
Draws a text of the pause menu at a place, turned for the vertical screen. With the third argument set it centers the text across the place (textDraw 0x500), else the text starts there (0x400).

The pause menu's Restart, in the practice mode: stops the sound, sets the continues of the players in the game to 0 and puts them in again (playerJoin), with new scores and lives, and requests the current scene again from its first part (stagePart 0).
The pause menu's Quit: stops the sound, adds the play time (playTimeAdd) and requests a save (saveRequest) when that returns 1, ends the game (gameDemoSet) and changes to the title (scene 4).
Opens Adjust Console from the pause menu: plays sound 0x46 and sets the menu's screen (byte 3) to 1.
Moves the pause menu's cursor up or down, round from end to end, with its sound.

The draw of the pause menu's task in list 6, which runs only while the game is paused: --- PAUSE MENU --- with Continue Game, Restart (only in the practice mode), Adjust Console and Quit, and a help line, for the player in pausePlayer. Adjust Console moves the screen's position by 4 with the directions, A or C sets it back to 0 and B goes back. When pausePlayer is 0 it resets the menu and ends the pause (pauseEnd).
Makes the pause menu's task in list 6 (pauseMenuDraw, removed by pauseHelpFreeBoth). stageStart calls it outside the attract demo and the tutorial.

Gives a player's ship its input for a frame from the recorded input (demoInput), held and newly pressed (playerInput). An entry is the input and a count n for n + 1 frames, or one byte with 0x80 set for one frame. After the recording's end the input is 0.
Sets the fog's stored setting (fogRed to fogFadeLevel) to a mix of two settings by a fraction: the color, held to 0 to 255, the near and far depths and the fade's level. fogFadeTask applies it.

The update of the task that fogFadeStart makes in list 5: each frame it moves the fraction on by 1/frames and mixes the fog (fogMix), and past 1 it takes the target setting and ends. Each frame it applies the setting: the fog's table, its color and the fade's level.
Makes the task that mixes the fog from one setting to another over a number of frames (fogFadeTask).
Moves the fog from its current setting to another over a number of frames. The stages change their fog with it.

Draws a ship's model at its motion's frame, in its polarity's color, flashing while invulnerable. It files the ship's hit record in list 0 unless forced or flags hold 0x08, and its field's in list 1 unless they hold 0x20 while byte 0x0f (unknown_0d[2]) is 0.
Draws a ship's field, the sprite of its polarity around it, its size from fieldGrowth with a random flicker.
Draws a ship in the camera's mode 0: through the camera path's position and angles, at (x, z, -y) (shipModelDraw).

Draws the two sprites of a new life's invulnerability, 0x11600 and the player's own (0x11601 or 0x11602), fading them out in the last 15 frames of Player.invulnerable. playerDrawFlat calls it while invulnerable is not 0.

Draws a ship in the camera's flat mode 1: at (x, y, z - depth), with its field (playerFieldDraw), its invulnerability's sprites while Player.invulnerable is not 0 (playerShieldDraw), and its model turned by 0x4000 about x and by Player.rotation about z (shipModelDraw).
Makes the shock ring (shockRingCreate, 31 segments) around a ship when it releases its homing lasers (playerButtons), in its polarity's color.
The task of shipsPushStart: while neither ship is out (state 4) and the two are closer than 6.25, it gives each a push away from the other (playerPushSet), the stronger the closer they are.
Makes the task that pushes the two ships apart (shipsPushApart), at stageStart.
Draws the spark of a dying ship (deathSparkCreate).

The update of a dying ship's spark (deathSparkCreate): while its size is above 2.5 it makes 4 particles a frame (effectParticles). It shrinks by 0.125 a frame down to 1.5, then fades out by 0x30 a frame and ends, and it takes a new random angle every second frame.
Makes the spark of a dying ship at its position, with particles.

Makes the effects of a ship's death at its position: a ring of 8 explosions (explosionRingKind2), an explosion burst (explosionBurst), its spark (deathSparkCreate) and a vibration of the player's controller (vibrationStart). playerUpdate calls it when the ship's hp is 0 or the ship lies in the scenery.
Sets the push that moves a ship (pushX, pushY).
Draws a shot's spark (shotSparkCreate).
The task of a shot's spark: moves it along y by its speed for two frames, steps its sprite once on the second frame, and ends on the third.
Makes the spark of a shot that hit, a sprite in the shot's color, from playerShotDraw.
Returns the first angle minus the second, wrapped to -0x7FFF to 0x8000.
Draws a release's flare at the side of the ship (releaseFlareCreate).
The task of a release's flare: shrinks it, then fades it out and ends.
Makes the flare at one side of a ship (0 or 1) when it releases its homing lasers, in its polarity's color. playerButtons makes the second side only with 20 energy or more.
Draws the sprite of playerTurnEffect at the ship, sized by the sine of its angle times 1.8.

The task of playerTurnEffect: it follows the ship while its sprite grows and its alpha rises to 100. Once the ship's flag 0x20 has been clear and is set again (its next turn), it fades the sprite out while it grows on, and ends. It ends at once when flag 0x04 is in the ship's flags or forced.
Draws the glow of absorbGlowCreate at the ship: sprite 0x10901, its size falling from 2.5 to 0 as its angle grows, its alpha the angle / 64 up to 0x50.
The task of an absorb's glow: follows the ship and ends on its 32nd frame, or at once when flag 0x04 is in the ship's flags or forced.

Makes the glow around a ship in its polarity's color, a task in list 2 (absorbGlowUpdate, absorbGlowDraw). playerAbsorb makes it when playerEnergy mod 10 plus the absorbed amount reaches 10, and not when the energy is already full.
Gives the camera a target view at once: its target and a blend of 1.

Moves the camera's blend to 0 over a number of frames (easeFloat), back from its target view to its own. The ease uses the camera's lock byte (unknown_1), so it waits for an earlier ease on that lock and holds it until it ends.
Draws a list of a bank's models, each at its own position, angles and scale.
Whether a slot of hitSlots holds an object whose removal has not started (used is 1). playerLaserUpdate checks its target with it.
Finds the bounds of a polygon's corners (Polygon).
Sets a polygon up with its corners and their count, and finds its bounds.
Sets a polygon's corners from others turned by an angle, and finds its bounds. The stages turn their scenery's outlines with it.

Makes the shock ring that closes in during a boss's destruction (shockRingCreate, 63 segments) at the boss's place: both radii start at its argument and one shrinks by a 24th of it each frame. bossDeathUpdate makes it at frame 152.

Makes the shock ring of a boss's explosion (shockRingCreate, 63 segments) at the boss's place: its radii start at 0 and at its argument and both grow by 4/75 of it each frame. bossDeathUpdate makes it when the boss explodes.

Draws a boss's destruction at the matrix that it keeps of the boss: two sprites 0x10A02 that grow and fade in until the vibration, then two sprites 0x10A00 that fade out. It also stores the matrix's position in stage coordinates for bossDeathUpdate (matrixTranslationStage).
Makes a player's controller vibrate at a boss's destruction.

The task of a boss's destruction. For 180 frames it copies the boss's matrix, pulls particles into it (chargeParticleCreate) and flashes the fade, then it vibrates the controllers, clears the enemies (enemiesClear), plays its sound and makes shock rings, explosion rings and particles. When its glow has faded out and 92 more frames have passed, it lowers the stage's lock (stageUnlock) and ends.

Starts a boss's destruction, a task in list 4 (bossDeathUpdate, bossDeathDraw) with level 0x81, so that the enemiesClear of bossDeathUpdate leaves it. It takes the boss's task, the address of the boss's matrix and a scale for the effects. The bosses' tasks call it 180 frames into their own explosions, one of them after 800 frames.

Sets the boss state at 0x8C1EA4AC. stageStart sets 0xFF, the stage programs 0 before their boss, and a boss's task 1 when the boss is destroyed. While it is 0, resultsStart gives no bonus for the boss time left. hudUpdate also tests it.
Draws a text of the results, its alpha from the object that it follows.
The task of a text of the results: ends with the object that it follows, or when that object's alpha reaches 0.

Makes a text at a place on the screen with a scale (resultsTextDraw), for resultsStep and remainBonusTask. It takes its alpha from byte 2 of its owner's data and ends with its owner (resultsTextUpdate).

Sets YOUR PLAY RANK (byte 1 of the results) to the number of entries in the rank table above the score. A player whose flag in playerNoShot is still set (no shot and no release since playerScoresClear) gets rank 0x0C instead, and two players get 0x0D only when both flags are set. Such a rank also counts up the player's byte in playerNoShotChapters.

The task of REMAIN BONUS: 91 frames after it starts it shows REMAIN BONUS, 46 frames later the PLAYER STOCK line, adds 500000 points for each life left of each player in the game (scoreAdd) and writes the new scores to chapterScores. After 151 more frames it fades its texts out and ends.

Unless the game is over, makes the task of REMAIN BONUS in list 0 (remainBonusTask) and sets stageEvents flags 0x02 and 0x08. On both ships it sets forced flags 0x02 and 0x08, clears their release and clears the shot, turn and release bits (0x10, 0x20, 0x40) of their input.
Places one quad of the HP gauge between two lengths (0 to 400) and gives its four corners one color, for the screen's orientation and optionScreenY.

When its state byte (0xC6) is 0, which hpGaugeSet sets, it places the HP gauge's three quads (hpGaugeBarPlace) from its values at 0xC0 and 0xC2, 400 to a full bar, in colors from the tables at 0x8C0D13FC and 0x8C0D1400. 92 frames later it sets the gauge back to one empty bar. It draws nothing: hpGaugeDraw calls it and then draws the quads.
A point that the current matrix transforms (matrixCalcPoint), with sceneCamera's depth added to its z: the point in the stage's coordinates.
The current matrix's position (matrixTranslation), with sceneCamera's depth added to its z: the position in the stage's coordinates.
Draws an enemy's model through a node tree (modelDrawNodeTree), with its color and its hit flash (enemyModelFlags).
Draws an enemy's model with a function for each node (modelDrawNodes), with its color and its hit flash (enemyModelFlags).
The common part of an enemy's destruction: an explosion with a ring of 8 more and particles (explosionBurst), its death bullets (enemyDeathBullets) and the kill for the chain (chainCount).
Draws the spark of an absorbed bullet (bulletAbsorb).
The task of an absorbed bullet's spark: pulls it toward its ship, shrinks it and lowers its alpha by 16 each frame. It ends below 16.
Fires a bullet that turns (bulletSpinCreate) at an angle with a speed.
Fires a bullet with a sprite (bulletSpriteCreate) at an angle with a speed.
bulletSpriteFireAt with sprite 0x10404.
bulletSpriteCreate with sprite 0x10508 and a velocity.
bulletSpriteFireAt with sprite 0x10508.
bulletSpriteFireAt with sprite 0x10504.
bulletFireAt with sprite 0x10308.
bulletFireAt with sprite 0x1030C.
Draws the burst where a ship absorbs part of a homing bullet (homingBurstCreate).
The task of a homing bullet's burst: each frame it lowers its alpha by 0x14 and grows its scale by 0.1. It ends when its alpha is below 0x15.
Makes a burst in a homing bullet's color at its position, with alpha 0xff and scale 0.25. homingBulletUpdate makes one each frame that the bullet's hit record shows a hit.
Draws a piece of a homing bullet's trail (homingTrailCreate).
The task of a piece of a homing bullet's trail: it lowers its alpha by 8 each frame and ends when its alpha is below 9.
Makes a piece of a homing bullet's trail at its position, in its color.
Draws a homing bullet (homingBulletCreate): its sprite and a glow sprite 0x10a02. It also files the bullet's hit record in hit list 4 (hitFile).

The task of a homing bullet. It slows by 0.05 per frame to its turning speed, then turns toward a lagging copy of its ship's position, with a turn rate that grows by 0x20 per frame up to its highest for 75 frames and then falls to 0. Within 0x400 of that direction its speed moves toward its straight speed, else toward its turning speed. Each frame that its hit record shows a hit, it gives 1 energy (playerAbsorb) and a push along its direction to the ship that hitBy bit 0x08 picks, and makes a burst (homingBurstCreate). When such a hit leaves it at 0 hit points, or once stageEvents has 0x02, it shrinks and fades. It ends outside x -32.5 to 32.5 or y -42.5 to 42.5.

Makes a homing bullet in list 4: white (0x11) or black (0x22), with 5 hit points, that homes on the ship that targetPlayerIndex picks for its position. The arguments: the color (0 white), the position, the highest turn rate, the angle, the turning speed, the straight speed and the first speed.
homingBulletCreate with a turn rate of 0x400, a turning speed of 0.625 and a straight speed of 0.925.

Draws a linkBulletCreate bullet: its sprite at its place, turned and stretched to span the bullets before and after it in its chain, and files its hit record, stretched the same way, in list 4. It also draws its spark (sprite 0x10900) while one is on.

The task of linkBulletCreate's bullets. It ends outside the play area. At 0 hit points a ship absorbed it: it moves next to that ship and calls bulletAbsorb. It vanishes (bulletVanish) when its owner's task ends, when it hits, or when stageEvents bit 0x02 clears the bullets. Else it drops the links to bullets that ended, moves, picks a new sprite and width every 2 frames, and with sparks on it sometimes starts a spark at a random point near it.

Makes a bullet in list 4 (linkBulletUpdate, linkBulletDraw) that moves at a speed along an angle, one of a chain: its sprite, one of 0x11000 to 0x1100F at random (to 0x11007 with bit 0x02 of the second argument), stretches to the bullet before it (the last argument), and the caller links the next one at 0xA8. Bits of the second argument: 0x08 clear gives it sparks, 0x10 raises its absorb value from 1 to 3.
Files a laser front's hit record in hit list 4 while its laser's alpha is 0xff, from the firing until the fade-out. Ends a front that is past the point where the laser stopped.

The task of a laser's front. It moves 2 units further along the laser each frame and raises the laser's length to its own distance. Scenery at its middle or at either side of the laser's width stops the laser there. A ship of its color absorbs it (playerAbsorb, 1 energy), gets a push and stops the laser there. It ends with its laser or outside x -35 to 35, y -45 to 45.
Makes a front at the origin of an enemy's laser, with a hit attribute and a step per frame, which finds how far the laser reaches. enemyLaserUpdate makes one each frame from the firing on.

Returns the length at which a laser from a point, at an angle, first comes within 5.5 of a player's ship, or comes nearest to it. It steps back from the given length by 2, then refines the length in halving steps. enemyLaserDraw cuts a laser to this length when the laser's byte 1 is set without bit 0x80.
Returns its float argument (fmov fr4,fr0). enemyLaserDraw calls it to keep a laser's length when the laser's byte 1 has bit 0x80.
Draws an enemy's laser (enemyLaserCreate) with its length from its fronts.

The task of an enemy's laser. It charges with particles for its charge frames, then fires along the angle that its angle pointer gives, with a shock ring unless flag 0x01 is set, and from then on sends a front each frame (laserFrontCreate). It fades and ends once its end byte reads 0x80, and ends at once when its owner's task ends.

Makes an enemy's laser in list 4. The arguments: its width, flags (0x01 fires without a shock ring), its hit attribute (0x11 white or 0x22 black), the owner's task, pointers to a position, an angle and an end byte, and its charge frames.
enemyLaserCreate with width 1.0 and 60 frames of charge.
enemyLaserCreate with width 0.5 and 60 frames of charge.
Fills an enemy's common part (enemyInitCommon), for an enemy that homing lasers cannot aim at.

Draws an enemy with a node tree (enemyTreeCreate): model 0x10002 at its motion frame through enemyModelDrawEach, unless flag 0x01 of byte 0x69 is set. When the model is in view and flag 0x02 is clear, it files the hit record in hit list 3 and draws a glow sprite 0x10a02 in its color.

The task of an enemy with a node tree (enemyTreeCreate). At 0 hit points it calls enemyDestroyed, plays one of 8 sounds and ends. Otherwise it runs its function at 0x74, ends when that returns nonzero, and else steps its motion by 2 frames unless flag 0x01 of byte 0x69 is set.
Frees an enemy's node tree when its task ends.

Makes an enemy in list 3 from a record with its position, angles and color (enemyInit), with 2 hit points, model 0x10002 and a node tree for it (modelNodeTreeCreate). It adds extra bytes of the given size at 0x7c, and the caller sets its function at 0x74.

Draws an enemy with model 0x10003 at a frame of its motion (enemyModel3Create). When the model is in view, it draws a glow sprite 0x10a02 in its color and, unless flag 0x02 of byte 0x69 is set, files the hit record in hit list 3.

The task of an enemy with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create). At 0 hit points it calls its function at 0x70 when set, calls enemyDestroyed, plays sound 8 (9 with flag 0x08 of byte 0x69) and ends. Otherwise it runs its function at 0x74, ends when that returns nonzero, and else steps its motion by 1 frame.

Makes an enemy in list 3 from a record with its position, angles and color (enemyInit), with 2 hit points, model 0x10003 and its motion at frame 0. It adds extra bytes of the given size at 0x7c, and the caller sets its function at 0x74.
Draws an enemy with model 0x10004 at a frame of its motion (enemyModel4Create). When the model is in view, it files the hit record in hit list 3 and draws a glow sprite 0x10a02 in its color.

The task of an enemy with model 0x10004 (enemyModel4Create). At 0 hit points it calls enemyDestroyed, plays sound 0xb and ends. Otherwise it runs its function at 0x70, ends when that returns nonzero, and else steps its motion frame by 1 for the motion in byte 0x69 with the step flags in byte 0x6a.

Makes an enemy in list 3 from a record with its position, angles and color (enemyInit), with 2 hit points, model 0x10004 and its motion 0 at frame 0, which wraps around. It adds extra bytes of the given size at 0x78, and the caller sets its function at 0x70.
Marks the tasks of lists 3 to 5 up to level 0x80 for removal and empties the hit lists.
The ship to aim at: the only ship in the game, else the nearer one (nearestPlayerIndex).
Turns an angle toward a target angle by at most a step, and returns it. Returns the target when it is within the step.
Turns an angle toward a ship from a point (aimAtPlayer), by at most a step (angleTurnToward).
Sets a point between two points by the cosine of an angle: the first point at angle 0, the second at 0x8000.
Returns 1 when the squared distance in x and y from a point to the ship of targetPlayerIndex is more than a value.
Draws a drift effect's sprite (effectDriftCreate), relative to the camera's depth unless flag 0x10 is set.
The task of a drift effect. It fades in, holds for its frames and fades out to its end. Each frame it moves by its velocity, which a factor scales, grows by 0.5%, turns, and steps its animation.

Makes a drift effect: an animated sprite (0x10200 to 0x10210, which then stays on 0x10210) that fades in, holds and fades out (effectDriftUpdate). Flag 0x01 makes it white, else black, and flag 0x10 puts it in list 0. The arguments: the flags, the position, the velocity, the angle and its turn, the fade-in step and the frames to hold (random when 0), the sprite's offset, the velocity's factor and the scale.

Makes a ring of explosions of a kind (effectExplosion) around a point: a number of them at even angles from a random start, at a radius with a random part, moving outward at a speed with a random part, plus a velocity.
explosionRing with explosions of kind 2.
explosionRing with explosions of kind 0x82.
An explosion with a ring of 7 more around it (explosionRingKind2), a shock ring (shockRingFire) and particles (effectParticles), of fixed sizes.

An explosion with a ring of a number of more around it (explosionRingKind2), a shock ring (shockRingFire) and particles (effectParticles). The first size scales the ring, the shock ring and the particles, the second the center explosion. enemyKill, playerDeathEffect and 11 unnamed functions call it.
effectFollow at a random angle, with one scale for x and y.
Draws a shock ring (shockRingCreate): its strip of quads with texture 0x10F00, at its position, turned by its three angles and scaled.
Writes a shock ring's vertices: its segments between the inner and the outer radius, with its alpha.

The task of a shock ring. It moves both radii by their steps and its scale by its factors, follows its position with flag 0x01, and after its frames changes its alpha by its step. It ends when the inner radius passes the outer one, when both are 0 or when its alpha runs out.
Frees a shock ring's vertex buffer when its task ends.
Makes a shock ring with a number of segments from a description (shockRingFire builds one), and its vertex buffer (syMalloc).

Makes a shock ring (shockRingCreate) at a position, drawn additively with the texture that the kind's low 6 bits offset from that of sprite 0x10F00, and following the position with bit 0x80 of the kind. Its outer radius starts at the seventh argument and grows by 5% of it each frame, its inner radius grows from 0 by 8% of it, and its scale starts at the fifth argument and is multiplied by the sixth each frame. Its alpha falls from 255 by 15 each frame after 15 frames.
Draws a sprite of a left band (leftBandSpriteCreate) with its alpha, at the band's sprite position.
The task of a left band's sprite: fades in to alpha 200 by 5 each frame, and once its band starts to fade out (byte 2 of the band) fades out by 5 each frame and ends below alpha 6.
Makes a sprite of a left band (leftBandUpdate makes 4).
Draws a left band's black quad, turned for a horizontal screen.

The task of a left band. It widens by 5 and its alpha rises by 5 each frame until alpha 200, holds for 182 frames, then fades out by 5 each frame and ends below alpha 6. It adds the 4 sprites from its first sprite id one by one at frames 32, 40, 48 and 56 (leftBandSpriteCreate).

Darkens a strip at the left of the screen, over its full height, with a black quad that widens to 205 (leftBandUpdate), and shows the 4 sprites from a sprite id at x 96, y 240. Five stage functions call it, with sprites of bank 4 or 8.
Draws a copy of a red band's sprite 0x11901 (redBandCopyCreate) with its alpha.

The task of a red band's copy. In 32 frames the copy moves and scales from its start to x 320, y 240 and scale 1, the band's middle, while its alpha rises by 10 to 120. Then it fades out by 10 each frame and turns back a little toward its start, raises the alpha of the band's sprites by 3 each frame up to 255, and ends at alpha 0.
Makes a copy of a red band's sprite 0x11901 at a start position and scale (redBandUpdate makes 8).

Draws a red band: its quad, turned for a horizontal screen, and while its alpha is not 0 the sprites 0x11900 and 0x11901 at its middle with that alpha, the second one shaken by up to 1 at random. While the band narrows, the two sprites shake apart sideways, further each frame.

The task of a red band. Its half height grows by 1.6 each frame to 72, its red pulses after 16 frames, and it makes a copy of its sprite every 4 frames for its first 32 frames (redBandCopyCreate). After 305 frames it narrows to nothing in 16 frames while its sprites stretch flat, shake apart and lose 20 of alpha each frame, and then ends.
Starts a vibration pattern on a player's controller (vibrationStart), for redBandCreate.

Shows a red band through the middle of the screen (redBandUpdate), plays the sound of its argument and sound 0x0F, and vibrates the controllers of the players in the game (redBandVibrate). The stage programs of chapters 1, 2 and 4 call it with command 9, and that of chapter 3 with command 14.
Draws a charge particle (chargeParticleCreate): sprites 0x10A02 and 0x10900 on alternate frames, black with flag 0x02, else white, on the screen's plane with flag 0x04.

The task of a charge particle. Its scale moves from 1 by its step each frame, and it sits at its distance times its scale from its matrix's center, at its angles, one of which turns. It ends at scale 0, when its stop byte is set or when its owner is marked for removal.

Makes a particle that moves into the center of a matrix as its scale falls (chargeParticleUpdate). The arguments: the flags, the owner's task, a stop byte, the matrix, two angles, the distance, the shrink each frame (varied by up to 0.005 at random) and the size. bossDeathUpdate, enemyLaserUpdate, chargeParticlePlayer and nine unnamed functions call it.
chargeParticleCreate on the screen's plane (flag 0x04), black or white by a ship's polarity. shipSideEffectUpdate calls it.
Starts a vibration pattern on a player's controller (vibrationStart), for shipSideEffectUpdate.
Sets playersInGame and gameOver to 0, gameDemo to 1 and soundOff to 0. gameOverTask, pauseQuit, gameTaskFrame and the unnamed endingTrialUpdate and endingFinish call it.
Sets the 6 rankPlaces to 0xFF, no place.
Sets menuItem, the second byte of menuPush, titleState and the depth of the title's menu stack to 0, and practiceItem to 5 times optionDifficulty, or 0 with USER SELECT (3).
Frees the text lines of one of a menu's two help buffers (menuHelpSet), and forgets the help that it shows.

Shows a menu's help of up to 2 lines: frees the buffer that is not shown and makes the lines' textures into it (textLineTexture). Does nothing while the help is the same, or while byte 0 of the menu's data is 0.
Draws a menu's help lines (menuHelpSet) at their place for the screen's orientation, over a polygon, except in titleState 2.
Draws the settings DIFFICULTY, EXTEND and PLAYER STOCK as text on the title.

Draws the title for titleTask. While byte 0 of its data is 1, it moves the black fade (byte 0x1C, fadeSet) toward byte 6 by 10 each frame and, unless the fade is 0xFF, draws sprite 0x20000 in one of three ways, with the settings (titleOptionsDraw) when bit 0x80 of byte 0x4D is set. It always draws the help (menuHelpDraw).
Saves menuItem, a second byte and titleState on the title's menu stack (menuPop restores them).
Restores menuItem, the second byte and titleState from the title's menu stack (menuPush).
Draws a menu's cursor: a character that turns at a position, and a translucent bar through it across the screen, blue or red (last argument), that pulses with a counter.

Moves the cursor menuItem[index] with up (0x10) or down (0x20) on the press of a given controller, wrapping between a lowest and a highest item, and plays sound 0x3F. When it moves it also sets byte 9 of its data, the cursor's counter, to 0 and returns 1.

Resets the state for a new game: both players' continues and polarities, the scores (playerScoresClear for 0, 1 and 2), gameTwoPlayers and gameFrames. It sets gamePrototype to 1 when optionPrototype is 1, and gameNoRanking to 1 in the practice, else 0. mainMenu and practiceMenu call it.
Makes the textures of the controller settings' 6 help lines (textLineTexture).
Frees the controller settings' 6 help lines.
Draws the controller settings' 6 help lines one under another, over a polygon, and frees the menu's help (menuHelpFree).
Steps a button setting through its 7 choices (buttonMasks) with left (0x40) or right (0x80) on a controller's press, wrapping, and plays sound 0x1A.

Changes the controller setting at a player's cursor: the shot, switch or release button (buttonChoiceStep), release with shot and switch together, or vibration. Vibration changes only with a vibration unit in one of the controller's sockets (pdVibIsReady).

The title's screen that asks whether to overwrite the data file on the card. YES (A or C) keeps the request in byte 0x0E of the title's data, NO or B clears it. Both return to the screen before (menuPop).
Frees the 16 text lines of the memory card check.
Shows a message of the memory card check: makes the textures of a number of lines from a table, each with its alignment and position (textLineTexture).
Draws the memory card check: sprite 0x20000 and its text lines.

The task of the memory card check at the boot. With a card in drive 0 it loads the data file (saveRead, optionsApply), or creates one (saveWrite) when it finds none and the card has 34 free blocks or more. It shows a message for each result (bootCardText), starts again when a card comes while it shows that there is none or goes while it shows a failure or too little space, and with START sets gameDemo to 1 and changes to scene 2.
Jumps to bootCardTextFree (a stub of mov.l and jmp). bootCardCreate makes it the destroy function of its task.
Starts the memory card check at the boot (bootCardUpdate). sceneBootStart calls it.

Prints the boot's text while the common data loads (textPrintf): the game's name, or its version while A is held on the second pad, then the copyright line and Now Loading. sceneBootStart calls it once.
Draws the logos' screen once bank 2 has loaded: sprite 0x20000 at the alpha in byte 4, and sprite 0x20100 at the alpha in byte 5 over a background of that gray level (njSetBackColor).

The task of the logos (sceneLogosStart). Once bank 2 has loaded, it shows the first logo for 182 frames while the screen fades in over 50, fades the logo out by 5 each frame, shows the second logo on a white background for 182 frames while the screen fades in over 90, fades to black over 50 frames, and 52 frames later requests the title (scene 4).
The removal of the logos' task: sets the background color back to black.

Draws the digits of a text as sprites 0x1180D to 0x11816, 32 apart in x, from the given position plus 320, 240. Other characters leave their place empty. modeSelectDraw draws the seconds left with it.
Loads bank 2 under the name MDSEL from the file list at 0x8C0D3C9C, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Draws the mode select's background: models 0x20000 and 0x20001 of bank 2 at the motion's frame, with the camera at 0x8C0D3C7C, turned for a horizontal screen.
The task of the mode select's background: scrolls the texture of its strips (uvStripsScroll) and steps the motion of model 0x20000.

Sets the mode select's light: its two angles, color 1, 1, 1 with intensity 0 and ambient 0.3. It sets the fog's color to 60, 70, 50 and the fade's level to 0.6, with byte 4 of ninjaFadeLevel at 1 so that drawFog uses Ninja's fade, and sets fogFadeOn.
Frees the block of strips (uvStripsFind) at the removal of the mode select's background task.
Makes the mode select's background (modeSelectLightFog): a task in list 0 that draws models 0x20000 and 0x20001 and scrolls the texture of a part of model 0x20001 (uvStripsFind).

Sets chapter 1's light (its two angles, color, intensity and ambient), and the fog's color to 200, 145, 100 and its depths (fogTableSet), with byte 4 of ninjaFadeLevel at 0 so that drawFog uses the fog, and sets fogFadeOn. Chapter 1's stage program calls it at its start.
Sets the main light's color, the three values that lightsReset sets to 1. Chapter 1's stage program calls it.

Sets chapter 1's light angles, the main light's color to 1, 1, 1 and the three values for the multi-light models to 0.5, 0.4, 0.3. It sets the fog's color to 120, 120, 120 and its depths (fogTableSet), with byte 4 of ninjaFadeLevel at 0, and sets fogFadeOn. Chapter 1's stage program calls it after enemiesClear.
Shows the left band with bank 4's sprites 0x40000 to 0x40003 (leftBandCreate). Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Loads bank 4 under the name S01_BG00 from the file list at 0x8C0DA968, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 5 under the name S01_BG01 from the file list at 0x8C0DAA28, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 2 under the name S01_OBJ00 from the file list at 0x8C0DA7C4, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 3 under the name S01_OBJ01 from the file list at 0x8C0DA884, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 6 under the name S01_BG02 from the file list at 0x8C0DAAD4, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 8 under the name S01_BG02B from the file list at 0x8C0DAB44, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 7 under the name S01_BG03 from the file list at 0x8C0DAB7C, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 3 under the name S01_BOSS from the file list at 0x8C0DABB8, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads banks 4 (S01_BG00) and 3 (S01_OBJ01) at once and bank 5 (S01_BG01) over frames. Chapter 1's stage program calls it at its start.
Frees bank 4 (bankFree). Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Frees bank 3 (bankFree). Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Loads banks 3 (S01_OBJ01) and 5 (S01_BG01) at once. Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Loads banks 2 (S01_OBJ00), 6 (S01_BG02) and 8 (S01_BG02B) over frames. Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Frees bank 5 (bankFree). Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Loads banks 2 (S01_OBJ00), 6 (S01_BG02) and 8 (S01_BG02B) at once and bank 7 (S01_BG03) over frames. Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Frees banks 2 and 6 (bankFree). Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Loads banks 8 (S01_BG02B) and 7 (S01_BG03) at once and bank 3 (S01_BOSS) over frames. Chapter 1's stage program calls it.
Plays sound 0x3A (soundPlay). Chapter 1's stage program calls it at scroll position 2000.

The movement of ch1Enemy01Spawn's enemies, with their data at Enemy.data. From its 23rd frame on it adds the x acceleration to the x velocity each frame and ends the enemy once it is out of view. In modes 1 and 2 the y velocity grows by 0.0015 each frame, and in mode 1 a change of the x velocity's sign cuts the acceleration to a quarter and starts mode 2. With its fire flag it fires one bullet of its color at a ship (bulletFire, aimAtPlayer with 2) when its frame count, from 0, equals its fire frame. It turns the enemy about z by its x velocity and moves it (enemyMove).
The behaviour of ch1Enemy01Spawn's enemies with a node tree: ch1Enemy01Move, and while the enemy lives it also turns it about y by its x velocity.
The behaviour of ch1Enemy01Spawn's enemies with model 0x10003: ch1Enemy01Move.

A stage script's record function of chapter 1, also called by ch1Enemy01WaveUpdate and chapter 3's ch3RingsWaveUpdate. Makes an enemy from the record: with a node tree (enemyTreeCreate) when record byte 0x3A is 0, else with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create). Its velocity comes from record words 6 to 8, its x acceleration from word 9, its mode from byte 0x39, and with byte 0x3B set its fire frame from byte 0x3C.

Draws a ch1Enemy02Create enemy: model 0x30000 at its motion's frame, and model 0x30001 on it with the second texture list when the enemy is black (attribute bit 0x02). While it is in view, it files its hit record in list 3.

The task of ch1Enemy02Create's enemies. At 0 hit points it calls enemyDestroyed, makes two more explosions when its motion is 1, plays sound 0x0C and ends. Else it runs its behaviour at 0x8C and ends when that returns nonzero, steps its motion and finds its firing point. After a shot (byte 0x68) it makes a muzzle flash there (effectFlash).
Makes an enemy in list 3 with 10 hit points and model 0x30000 of bank 3, with extra bytes of the given size at 0x94 (ch1Enemy02Update, ch1Enemy02Draw). The caller sets its behaviour at 0x8C.
Draws model 0x30000 at its motion's frame, with the second texture list when byte 2 is set, and keeps in byte 1 whether it was out of view.
The task of ch1ModelPassCreate's model: moves it by its velocity, turns it by its x velocity and steps its motion. It ends once it is out of view above y 0.

A stage script's record function of chapter 1: makes model 0x30000 of bank 3 without a hit record in list 4, at the record's position with the record's velocity (ch1ModelPassUpdate, ch1ModelPassDraw).
Draws model 0x30000 at its position without the camera's depth, at its motion's frame, with the second texture list when byte 2 is set, and keeps in byte 1 whether it was out of view.

The task of ch1ModelRiseCreate's model. Once the scroll has stopped and its wait has passed, it plays motion 1 once when x is at most 115, else motion 2. It then rises by 0.25 each frame, its x speed changes by 0.025 each frame toward x 115, and its z speed by 0.025 in its direction. It turns about z by its x speed and ends when it is out of view above y -120. Its z moves by its z speed all the time.

A stage script's record function of chapter 1: makes model 0x30000 of bank 3 without a hit record in list 0, at the record's position with 30 added to z (ch1ModelRiseUpdate, ch1ModelRiseDraw). Record byte 0x39 gives its wait in steps of 32 frames, and byte 0x3A the direction of its z speed.

A behaviour of ch1Enemy02Spawn: adds its x acceleration each frame and brings the y velocity up toward -0.375 by 0.0125, turned by its x velocity. On hard, or with record byte 0x3E set, it fires five bullets of its color, one every 4 frames from its 17th frame (bulletSpriteFireAt10508). It ends below y 0 once out of view.
Starts ch1Enemy02Move0: takes the x acceleration from record word 9 and picks motion 1 or 2 by its sign.

A behaviour of ch1Enemy02Spawn: slows by a factor of 0.95 each frame for 18 frames. It then turns toward a ship (angleTurnTowardPlayer) and keeps slowing for 16 times record byte 0x3A plus 2 frames. In that time it fires a bullet of its color every 4 frames, from the 69th frame until 16 times that byte minus 16 frames have passed. It then turns for 62 more frames and speeds away to its side and up until it is out of view.
Starts ch1Enemy02Move1: picks motion 1 when it starts at x above 0, else motion 2, and plays it backwards from motion 1's last frame.

A behaviour of ch1Enemy02Spawn: swings from side to side about a centre (record word 10) with an amplitude (record word 9), its phase growing by 16 times record byte 0x3B each frame, while its y velocity rises toward -0.1 and y moves by twice it. Every 4 frames it fires a bullet of its color downward (bulletSpriteCreate10508): in the middle part of its swing when record byte 0x3F is 0, else near its ends. It ends below y 0 once out of view.
Starts ch1Enemy02Move2: its phase from record byte 0x3A, and motion 1 or 2 by whether that phase lies between a quarter and three quarters of a turn and by its direction.

A stage script's record function of chapter 1: makes a ch1Enemy02Create enemy with its velocity from record words 6 to 8 and, by record byte 0x39, one of three behaviours (ch1Enemy02Move0 to Move2) with its init (ch1Enemy02Init0 to Init2).

Draws two flickering glow sprites, 0x10A03 or 0x10A02 on alternate frames and 0x10A02 at alpha 0x78, at each of the two points of the table at 0x8C0D48C0, with flags 0x840000 or 0x800000 by bit 0 of its argument. ch1TreeModelDraw and ch1Enemy03Draw call it.
A node function of ch1TreeModelCreate's tree: draws model 0x30003 there, with the second texture list when byte 1 of the model's data is set.

Draws model 0x30002 through its node tree at its position without the camera's depth, at its frame of motion 2, with the second texture list when byte 1 is set. While it is in view, it draws the glows of ch1GlowPairDraw.
The task of ch1TreeModelCreate's model: moves it by 0.1 in z each frame and steps its motion 2. It ends once the scroll has stopped and the model is out of view.
Frees the node tree at the removal of ch1TreeModelCreate's task.

A stage script's record function of chapter 1: makes model 0x30002 of bank 3 without a hit record in list 0, with a node tree (modelNodeTreeCreate) of which one node draws model 0x30003 (ch1TreeModelNodeDraw).

The task of ch1Enemy03Pair. While the scroll is at most 2100, it waits until its count, 4 at the start and lowered by ch1Enemy03Update at each death of the pair's enemies and of the enemies they make in their place, is 0, then calls ch1SwayWave and ends. It ends without the call once the scroll passes 2100.
A stage script's record function of chapter 1: makes two ch1Enemy03Create enemies from the two records at 0x8C0D48D8, and a task that counts their deaths (ch1Enemy03PairWatch).
A node function of ch1Enemy03Create's tree for type 0: draws model 0x30003 there, with the second texture list by byte 0xB8 of its argument.
A node function of ch1Enemy03Create's tree for type 1: draws model 0x30004 there, with the second texture list by byte 0xB8 of its argument.

Draws a ch1Enemy03Create enemy: model 0x30002 through its node tree (enemyModelDrawEach), and while it is in view the glows of ch1GlowPairDraw and its hit record in list 3. While the size at 0x1B0 is above 0, it also draws sprite 0x10608 at that size at each of its first four firing points, a quarter turn apart from the angle at 0x1B4 (both set by ch1Enemy03Move0).

The behaviour of type 0 of ch1Enemy03Create. It moves in to record words 6 to 8, then repeats a cycle: a wait, two volleys 64 frames apart from firing points 4 to 18 (bulletFireAt10308, effectFollowScaled, sound 0x12), and 8 rounds of sprite bullets from its first four points (bulletSpriteFireAt10508, sound 0x103) with the sprites of ch1Enemy03Draw. When a cycle ends after the scroll passes 2000, it moves out to its side and ends out of view.

Starts type 0 of ch1Enemy03Create: behaviour ch1Enemy03Move0, two enemies of its color that circle it on opposite sides (ch1OrbiterCreate), and a phase step of 0x60 per frame for its move in, or 0x120 with record byte 0x3E.

The task of ch1RingCreate's centre in list 4. It turns the ring each frame and first eases the centre's x to 0. When its enemy dies (ch1Enemy03Update), the ring turns faster, widens to 34, moves to record words 6 to 8 and narrows to 26. After the scroll passes 3800 it widens past 40 and the task ends. If the scroll passes 3500 before that death, the centre rises and the task ends past y 90.
Makes the centre of a ring (ch1RingUpdate) in list 4 at a record's position, and 12 enemies around it at even angles (ch1RingEnemyCreate), in alternating colors by threes.
Places a ring's enemy at its place on the ring: the ring's centre plus its radius, turned by the ring's angle plus the enemy's own, with y scaled by a constant.
The behaviour of a ring's enemy: follows its place on the ring (ch1RingEnemyPlace) with the move as its velocity, and ends when the ring's centre is removed.
Makes an enemy with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create) on a ring at an angle and in a color, which follows its place (ch1RingEnemyBehaviour).

The behaviour of type 1 of ch1Enemy03Create. It moves in to record words 6 to 8 and starts to spin. Then it fires a laser from its firing point along its spinning angle (enemyLaserFire) with sequence 0x10C. 61 frames after the shot it plays sound 0x10A, and 258 frames after the shot it fades that sound out, ends the laser and rises until it ends out of view.
Starts type 1 of ch1Enemy03Create: behaviour ch1Enemy03Move1 and a ring of 12 enemies (ch1RingCreate) from a fixed record, whose centre it keeps at 0x1BC.

The task of ch1Enemy03Create's enemies. It drops its ring and its pair once their tasks end. At 0 hit points it stops its sounds, calls enemyKill, plays sound 0x0D and ends. With a ring it first marks the ring's centre. Else, when it has a pair, it lowers the pair's count and, when record byte 0x3E is 0 and the scroll is before 1850, makes a new enemy of the pair from its record with that byte set to 1. While it lives, it turns toward a ship at its turn rate (0x78) when it has no ring, places its firing points, runs its behaviour at 0x1B8, sets the pan and volume of its one-shot sound from its first firing point and steps its motion.
Frees the node tree at the removal of ch1Enemy03Create's task.
Makes an enemy in list 3 with 120 hit points, model 0x30002 of bank 3 with a node tree and a copy of its record, and starts its type by record byte 0x3F (ch1Enemy03Init0, ch1Enemy03Init1).
Places an enemy on a circle: its data's centre plus its radius turned by its angle (sine for x, cosine for y), at the centre's z.

The behaviour of ch1OrbiterCreate's enemies: they circle their owner, turning by 0x100 each frame in the direction that their color picks. Once the owner's step (byte 0x69) is 2 or more, they fire a bullet at a ship every 128 frames (bulletFire, aimAtPlayer). When the owner's task ends, the centre of their circle rises at a growing speed, and they end out of view.
Makes an enemy with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create) that circles an owner from an angle (ch1OrbiterBehaviour), in a color.

The behaviour of ch1CirclerCreate's enemies: their circle's centre moves to record words 6 to 8 in 256 frames. Then 6 times they wait 34 frames and make a half turn. As 3 of these turns start, picked by their color, they fire a bullet at a ship (bulletFire, aimAtPlayer). Then they fly off. After the move in, they end once out of view.
A stage script's record function of chapter 1: makes an enemy with model 0x10003 that circles about a point from its record (ch1CirclerBehaviour), from the angle in record byte 0x39.

The task of ch1Enemy01Wave: makes three ch1Enemy01Spawn enemies from its record, one every 21 frames. Then, while the scroll is at or before 1150, it mirrors the record's x and x acceleration, switches the color and starts again. Else it ends.

A stage script's record function of chapter 1: makes a task (ch1Enemy01WaveUpdate) that sends waves of ch1Enemy01Spawn enemies down from y 40, starting at x 20 or -20 on the side away from the ship that targetPlayerIndex picks.
