Side 0 then starts sequence 0x102. Every fourth frame it fires a fan of 8 bullets of both colors in turn (bulletSpriteFireAt10404) at 1.75. The fan narrows from 0x1400 to 0xA00 between bullets over 160 frames while it turns from the aim to angle 0x9400 (side 0) or 0x6C00, then sways 0xC00 to both sides of that angle.

The first phase of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossUpdate step 2). The boss sways in a figure eight about y 38, up to 2.5 out. On the boss's 61st frame its four parts can be hit, the boss timer starts and it makes two drones (ch5BossDrone1). From then on it fires three streams in the parts' colors, from a random one of a part's four points, every 4, 12 or 20 frames (hard, normal, easy), 4 frames more for each lost ship up to 20. Two streams go round the four parts and fire only from the destroyed ones: one at angles 0x6000 to 0x9FFF, and one twice as often at 0x7000 to 0x8FFF. The third fires at 0x7000 to 0x8FFF from all four parts in turn. 794 frames after the drones, and then every 193 frames, it also fires a homing bullet (homingBulletCreate) from the next live part in its color, with sound 0x101. A lost ship delays that bullet by 384 frames.

The behaviour of chapter 5's boss's drones in the second phase (ch5BossDroneCreate). It moves in from z 20 to its place, x 25 (side 0) or -25 at y 16, over 128 frames. Every 17, 33 or 97 frames (hard, normal, easy) it fires 5 bullets at 0.325 to 0.375, white for side 0 and black for side 1, up to 0x800 to one side of its aim. It turns every second round by 0xC00 to 0x1BFF, each time the other way, and side 0 starts with such a round. It turns its aim toward a ship by 0x80 a frame. Side 0 starts half an interval earlier.

The second phase of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossUpdate step 5). The boss sways in a figure eight about y 35, up to 2.5 out, and keeps its move of the frame at 0x2C for the missiles. On the phase's 61st frame its two parts can be hit and the boss timer starts. On the next frame the parts start to fire missiles in turn, one every 257 frames (ch5BossMissileCreate): the first part black at angle 0x6000, the second white at 0xA000, while it lives. 384 frames after the parts open it makes two drones (ch5BossDrone2).

The behaviour of chapter 5's boss's drones in the third phase (ch5BossDroneCreate). It moves from x -25 (side 0) or 25, y 32.5, z 20 to x -17.5 or 17.5, y 27.5, z 0 over 128 frames. Then it fires one bullet at 0.5 every 4, 8 or 12 frames (hard, normal, easy), black for side 0 and white for side 1, at a random angle from 0x17FF to one side of its aim to 0x2800 to the other. It turns its aim toward a ship by 0x80 a frame.
A glow at chapter 5's boss's fire point at 0x180 (effectFollow with flag 0x80): kind 7 (white) with 0, else kind 4 (black), at a random angle.

The third phase of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossUpdate step 8). The boss sways in a figure eight about y 15, up to 2.5 out, and fires from 20 above it (0x180). On the phase's 61st frame the core can be hit and the boss timer starts. From 63 frames after that it fires two mirrored streams on every second frame that sweep from angle 0x2600 to 0xD600 (bulletFireAt1030c). 262 frames after the core opens it makes two drones (ch5BossDrone3). On the next frame it fires its first lasers (ch5BossLaserFan), 81 frames later the next, then 2 frames sooner each time, down to 29, 45 or 49 frames (hard, normal, easy). 16 frames before each fan after the first the core spins 1.5 turns, and it changes its color halfway. Once the gap is below 55, it also fires fans at a ship every third of the gap: 10 bullets, then 9, at 0.375, with a spread that each 9-bullet fan narrows. A lost ship lengthens the gap by 24 frames up to 81 and resets the spread.

The task of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossCreate), in 11 steps, with three phases of an 80-second boss timer each. Its fire value starts at 4, 2 or 0 (easy, normal, hard), is set to 3, 2 or 0 for phase 3, and grows by 1 with each lost ship, up to 4. Phase 1 (ch5BossPhase1) ends when its four parts or the timer are gone. Each part bursts at 0 hit points (explosionBurst, sound 0x0D). At the end of each phase the drones explode (byte 0x0B). The boss then shows ch5BossOverlay2, bursts (ch5BossBurst) with sound 0x0D, the bullets vanish, and it moves to y 35 over 256 frames. Phase 2 (ch5BossPhase2) ends the same way with its two parts. A destroyed part also makes the bullets vanish, explodes the missiles (byte 0x13A), fires a last missile and lets the other part fire next. Then the boss shows ch5BossOverlay3 and bursts, the bullets vanish, the missiles explode and the music stops. It moves to y 15 over 256 frames and starts music 8 (sequencePlay) on the move's 8th frame. Phase 3 starts once its node tree's motion has also ended. Phase 3 (ch5BossPhase3) ends when the core or the timer is gone, and a destroyed core sets the boss state (bossStateSet 1). Then it bursts with sequence 0x13, stops sound 0x103, lowers the stage's lock (stageUnlock), makes the bullets vanish and sets flag 0x40 (no shots) on both ships. Then it spins, drifts to the centre and moves by z -0.25 a frame, with explosions on every second frame for 300 frames, and makes its destruction (bossDeathCreate) on the 181st frame.
Frees the node tree at the removal of chapter 5's boss's task and makes the next task (ch5FinalCreate).

Makes chapter 5's boss in list 3 (ch5BossUpdate, ch5BossDraw) with a node tree of model 0x30000 (node functions ch5BossNodeParts, ch5BossNodePart2A and ch5BossNodePart2B) and a shape buffer (njInitShape). Hit records: an armoured white body at 0x384 for the first phase, the first phase's parts at 0x284 to 0x344 (black, white, white, black) with 400 hit points on easy, else 600, an armoured body at 0x444 for the second phase, the second phase's parts at 0x3C4 (black) and 0x404 (white) with 600 or 800, and the white core at 0x484 with 4000 or 6000. It starts at y 38, z -17.5, turned half a turn, and keeps the arrival's sound slot. ch5BossArrivalUpdate makes it.

Draws chapter 5's boss's arrival: its node tree (model 0x30000) turned half a turn about y and pitched by 0x18, the core (model 0x30006) at node 20's matrix, and the four parts (model 0x30003, black for parts 0 and 3) at node 1's matrix.

The task of chapter 5's boss's arrival (ch5BossArrivalCreate). After 400 frames it starts sequence 0x104. It then rises from y -200 to 42.5 over 357 frames, and in the rise's second half its z goes from -16510 to -16548. From the frame of the sequence to the rise's 267th frame it makes drift effects (effectDriftCreate) on every second frame. It plays sound 0x103 and levels out over 213 frames. Once stageLocks[12], the lock of the camera eases of ch5ShipsUpdate, is 0, it sets the camera's mode to 1, makes the boss (ch5BossCreate), lowers the stage's lock (stageUnlock) and ends.
The function of node 1 of chapter 5's boss's arrival: keeps its matrix at 0x24.
The function of node 20 of chapter 5's boss's arrival: keeps its matrix at 0x64.
Frees the node tree at the removal of chapter 5's boss's arrival task.

Makes chapter 5's boss's arrival in list 0 (ch5BossArrivalUpdate, ch5BossArrivalDraw) with a node tree of model 0x30000, at y -200, z -16510, pitched 0x1000. Chapter 5's stage program calls it at scroll position 14500.

Draws a laser of chapter 5's boss: files its hit record in list 4 while it homes, and draws its trail of up to 16 points as a strip (flags 0x870000 white, 0x810000 black). When its hit record shows a hit, as when it hits a ship or a field absorbs it, it starts its end.

The task of a laser of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossLaserCreate). From its 10th frame it homes on a ship (targetPlayerIndex): it turns in the direction it first picked, faster each frame up to 0x1000, and eases in once it faces the ship. Within 0x2800 of the ship's direction its speed grows 1.25 times a frame up to 2.75, else it drops 0.925 times a frame down to 0.75. A ship of its color absorbs it for 10 energy (playerAbsorb). A hit on a ship stops its homing, and its draw then starts its end. When its ship is gone it flies straight and ends outside x -30 to 30, y -40 to 40. Its trail grows to 16 points and shrinks at its end. When the bullets vanish it ends with a flash.

Makes a laser of chapter 5's boss in list 4 (ch5BossLaserUpdate, ch5BossLaserDraw) at a position, with an attribute (0x11 white, 0x22 black), an angle and a speed: a hit record of 10 hit points and power 10, and a trail of 16 points.
Draws a laser charge of chapter 5's boss at the core's point of its index: its sprite at its scale and angle, white or black, and sprite 0x10A02 while it charges.

The task of a laser charge of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossLaserChargeCreate). Sprite 0x10903 shrinks from 1.6 by 0.1 a frame. On the 16th frame it starts the laser (ch5BossLaserCreate) at its point at 0.75, with sound 0x102 for index 0. Then sprite 0x10900 starts at 4 and each frame shrinks to 0.75 times its size at a new random angle. The task ends once its size is 0.5 or less. It ends at once when the bullets vanish.
Makes a laser charge of chapter 5's boss in list 4 (ch5BossLaserChargeUpdate, ch5BossLaserChargeDraw) from the boss, an index of the core's points, an attribute and an angle.

Draws a drone of chapter 5's boss: its node tree (model 0x30001) at its motion's frame, turned by 0x2C and 0x30, files its hit record, and draws glow sprite 0x10A02 at its node: white for byte 0x14 = 0, black for 1, both for 2.

The task of a drone of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossDroneCreate): runs its behaviour (0xE0), which ends it with a non-zero result, steps its motion and turns it by 0x200 a frame. A lost ship raises its fire value by 1, up to 4. When the boss sets byte 0x0B, it explodes (enemyExplosion 0xC2) and ends.
The function of node 5 of a drone of chapter 5's boss: keeps its matrix at 0x60 and places its fire point at 0x34 on the play field.
Frees the node tree at the removal of a drone of chapter 5's boss and stops its sequence (byte 6).

Makes a drone of chapter 5's boss in list 3 (ch5BossDroneUpdate, ch5BossDroneDraw) with a node tree of model 0x30001 and an armoured white hit record of 1 hit point. It takes the boss, a behaviour (ch5BossDrone1, ch5BossDrone2 or ch5BossDrone3), a side and a glow color. Its fire value starts at 4, 2 or 0 (easy, normal, hard). It calls the behaviour once.

Draws a missile of chapter 5's boss: model 0x30002, black with flag 0x10000, turned by its angle and roll, files its hit record, and draws its engine (sprites 0x10900 and 0x10708 to 0x1070B) once it is lit.

The task of a missile of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossMissileCreate). For 62 frames it moves with the boss at half its low speed, and on the 62nd it lights its engine. It homes on its ship's smoothed position: its turn rate grows by 0x20 a frame up to 0x400, and after 511 frames drops by 0x10 a frame. Its speed swings between its two speeds every 128 frames. Every 4 units of flight it drops a mine of its color (ch5BossMineCreate). It explodes (enemyExplosion 0xC2) when it hits something or when the boss sets byte 0x13A. After 512 frames it ends outside x -32.5 to 32.5, y -42.5 to 42.5. With flag 0x80 it starts at once, swings every 256 frames, keeps turning and only ends by explosion.

Makes a missile of chapter 5's boss in list 4 (ch5BossMissileUpdate, ch5BossMissileDraw) at a position, with an angle and a low and a high speed, aimed at a ship (targetPlayerIndex): black with flag 1, else white, with an armoured hit record of 1 hit point. Flag 0x80 marks the last missile of a destroyed part.
Draws a mine of chapter 5's boss: its sprite at its depth, angle and alpha, and files its hit record in list 4 while it is not fading.

The task of a mine of chapter 5's boss (ch5BossMineCreate). It shows sprites 0x11000 to 0x11007 in turn every second frame. After its frames it fades out by 15 a frame and ends. At 0 hit points a ship absorbs it (bulletAbsorb 2). In the scenery, when hit or when the bullets vanish it vanishes (bulletVanish). It ends outside the play field.

Makes a mine of chapter 5's boss in list 4 (ch5BossMineUpdate, ch5BossMineDraw): a standing bullet of an attribute (0x11 white, 0x22 black) with 1 hit point, at a position, with an angle and a number of frames. ch5BossMissileUpdate drops them for 384 frames.

Shows seven screen sprites (screenSpriteFade): 0x50100 and 0x50101 at once for 300 frames, 28 to the left, 0x50102 and 0x50103 after 45 frames for 255, 68 to the left, 0x50104 after 90 frames for 210, and 0x50105 and 0x50106 after 125 frames for 175, 64 to the left. ch5FinalUpdate calls it before the last fight's object moves in.
Shows screen sprites 0x5000A and 0x5000B (screenSpriteFade) at once for 300 frames, 32 to the left. They blink. ch5FinalUpdate calls it while its object charges.
linkBulletCreate with no owner, flags 0x11 (absorb value 3) and 2.0 as its sixth argument, from an attribute, a position, a speed, an angle and the bullet before it in the chain.
Sets the fire value (byte 4) of chapter 5's last fight: 2 on easy, 1 on normal, 0 on hard.
Returns the angle from a point to the middle of both ships when both play, else to the one ship that plays, else to the origin.

Makes a shock ring (shockRingCreate) that follows the path point of chapter 5's last fight (0x120), with a size: its inner radius from 0 and its outer radius from the size both grow by 4/75 of the size each frame, and its alpha falls from 255 by 17 each frame after 61 frames.

Makes a shock ring (shockRingCreate) at the path point of chapter 5's last fight (0x120) with a size: its inner radius shrinks from the size by 1/24 of it each frame, its scale grows by 1.05 times each frame, and its alpha rises from 0 by 10 each frame.

Makes a shock ring (shockRingCreate) that follows the object of chapter 5's last fight: its outer radius starts at 12.5 and grows by 0.078125 each frame, and its alpha falls from 255 by 8 each frame after 16 frames.

The first pattern of chapter 5's last fight (ch5FinalUpdate step 5). Until frame 1141, every fourth frame it fires 8 black and 8 white bullets (bulletSpriteFireAt10508) 5 out from itself, 0x2000 apart. The black angles turn by 0x200 a round to a random side, the white ones are mirrored. Their speeds go up in rounds of four. Each four rounds the step of the speeds falls from 0.025 by 0.0005 and their base rises from 0.425 by 0.005, up to 0.575. It counts the step's frames.

The second pattern of chapter 5's last fight (ch5FinalUpdate step 6). After 60 frames it moves in turn to a random place at y 20 to 25: from x 0 or less to x 7.5 to 17.5, else to x -17.5 to -7.5. Each move slows into place over 0x4000/speed frames, with a speed of 0x100 (0x180 on hard) that grows by 0x10 before each move, up to 0x200. After each move it fires two rings 32 frames apart, each of 34 pairs of spiral bullets (ch5FinalSpiralBullet) whose two bullets turn opposite ways: the first at 0.3 in a color picked at random at the start, the second at 0.7 in the other color. A lost ship slows the moves by 0x100, down to 0x80. It aims the chain fan at the ships (ch5FinalAim) and counts the step's frames.

The third pattern of chapter 5's last fight (ch5FinalUpdate step 7). It moves to x 0, y 22.5 over 128 frames while the chain fan turns from the ships to angle 0x8000. Then every 64 frames it fires a ring of spiral bullets (ch5FinalSpiralBullet) at 0.25 from 10, 20 or 30 angles (easy, normal, hard), with two bullets at each angle that turn opposite ways, two angles white and two black in turn. Each ring has 2 angles more. A lost ship takes 16 angles away, down to 10. It picks the fan's spin direction (byte 0xAD) and counts the step's frames.

Draws the object of chapter 5's last fight: on the stage path in camera mode 0, at its position in camera mode 1, where it also files its hit record while byte 0x85 is set. It keeps its matrix at 0x24 until byte 0x14 is set, and draws models 0x40000, 0x40001 and 0x40002 (the last two until byte 0x84 is set) at their motions' frames. While byte 7 is set it draws its glow sprite (0x0C) at the scale at 0x10 and the alpha of byte 8, and sprite 0x10900 at the scale at 0x20 while that is above 0.
Makes a charge particle (chargeParticleCreate) into the matrix of chapter 5's last fight at 0x24, at the distance at 0x18 with the shrink at 0x1C, that stops when byte 0x14 is set.
Makes a player's controller vibrate (vibrationStart) with a fixed pattern for time 0x24.

The task of chapter 5's last fight (ch5FinalCreate), in 13 steps. It starts sequence 0x100, which pans with it, and waits for stage part 2. Then it starts a 60-second boss timer and sequence 0x10B, shows ch5FinalOverlay1 after 90 frames, and moves from z -20 to y 22.5 over 256 frames. It charges for 150 frames (ch5FinalCharge, ch5FinalOverlay2), then starts the timer, a ring (ch5FinalRingStart) and sequence 0x104. Its patterns follow: ch5FinalSpirals for 1200 frames, ch5FinalMoveRings for at least 1200 more, then ch5FinalRingWaves for 1080 with sequence 0x108 at their end. From frame 400 of the spirals to the end of the second pattern it fires orbs (ch5FinalOrb) every 7, 13 or 25 frames (hard, normal, easy). From the second pattern on, which starts with a shock ring and sequence 0x105, every 5 frames it fires a fan of 4 (easy) or 6 chains of linked bullets (ch5FinalChainBullet) in both colors, which spreads and then spins from the third pattern on. A lost ship raises its fire value, and at 3 the orbs stop. When the timer ends it stops its sounds and fire, fades out its glow and after 90 frames the music, lowers the stage's lock (stageUnlock) and rises to y 57.5 over 1024 frames. When ch5CloseRingRequest is set it makes a closing ring (ch5FinalRingClose). At stage part 4 it stops all sounds, vibrates the controllers (ch5FinalVibrate), makes a ring (ch5FinalRingEnd), and on its third frame starts sequence 0x103 and music 9 (sequencePlay) and makes rings of explosions (explosionRing) at its path point. It keeps a pointer to its position at ch5FinalPosition.

Makes the object of chapter 5's last fight in list 3 (ch5FinalUpdate, ch5FinalDraw) with level 0x81, which enemiesClear leaves, and an armoured white hit record of 0xFFFF hit points. It loads sound banks (soundLoadBanks) and sets finalFight, so that playerAbsorb gives only score. ch5BossDestroy calls it.

Draws a ch5FinalSpiralBullet inside the play field: its sprite (0x1030C plus its frame) at its depth, which white and black swap every frame, and files its hit record. While its radius is below 12.5, white and black bullets show and file only on alternate frames.

The task of a ch5FinalSpiralBullet: its radius about its centre grows by its speed and its angle by its turn each frame, and its frame steps every second frame. At 0 hit points it is absorbed (bulletAbsorbed). When hit or when the bullets vanish, it vanishes (bulletVanish). It ends outside the play field and its margin of 60, at x -90 to 90, y -100 to 100.

Makes a bullet of chapter 5's last fight in list 4 (ch5FinalSpiralBulletUpdate, ch5FinalSpiralBulletDraw) that circles out from a centre: an attribute with 1 hit point, the centre, a start angle, a turn each frame and a speed. Its radius starts at 5.
Draws a ch5FinalOrb: sprite 0x10A00 at its size and angle, with a depth that white and black swap every frame, and glow sprite 0x10A02 at its glow's size. It files its hit record once it has stopped.

The task of a ch5FinalOrb. It slows by 0.925 times each frame while its size grows by 0.0125 up to 0.6 and its glow by 0.05 up to 0.75. Once grown and slower than 0.1 it stops, and its sprite narrows by 0.05 a frame down to a width of 0.15 while it aims at a ship (aimAtPlayer). Then it speeds up to its top speed. At 0 hit points it is absorbed (bulletAbsorbed). When hit or when the bullets vanish, it vanishes (bulletVanish). It ends outside the play field.

Makes an orb of chapter 5's last fight in list 4 (ch5FinalOrbUpdate, ch5FinalOrbDraw): an attribute with 1 hit point, a position, an angle, a start speed, a top speed and a speed-up each frame. ch5FinalUpdate fires them at 0.25 to 3.75, with a top speed of 0.725 and a speed-up of 0.025.
The task of stageUnlockAfter: counts its frames down, and at 0 it ends and lowers the stage's lock (stageUnlock).
Makes a task in list 0 with no draw (stageUnlockAfterUpdate) that lowers the stage's lock after a number of frames.

Shows five screen sprites (screenSpriteFade), each for 220 frames: 0x50107 at once, 0x50108 and 0x50109 after 250 frames, 28 to the left, and 0x5010A and 0x5010B after 500 frames, 24 to the left. It lowers the stage's lock after 780 frames (stageUnlockAfter).

Draws one ship of ch5Ships that takes part at the sequence's place and angles for it: on the stage path in camera mode 0, in the play field in camera mode 1. It keeps that matrix for its side effects and draws the ship's model (shipModelDraw) while the ship's state is below 3 and forced flag 0x04 is set.
The draw of ch5Ships: both ships (ch5ShipsDrawOne).
Moves one ship of ch5Ships from its start to its target place and angles by the cosine of the sequence's phase (pointBlendCos).
Moves both ships of ch5Ships (ch5ShipsBlendOne), and returns 1 once the phase reaches 0x8000.
Makes a shock ring (shockRingCreate, 31 segments) at a ship of ch5Ships, with a texture by its argument.
Makes a second kind of shock ring (shockRingCreate, 31 segments) at a ship of ch5Ships, with a texture by its argument.

Sets the first move of one ship of ch5Ships that takes part, from its position and angles to a place and angles by its order (the tables at 0x8C107B30 and 0x8C107B48), and makes its two side effects (shipSideEffectCreate). It sets forced flag 0x04 in any case.
Slows one ship of ch5Ships that takes part by 0.025 a frame down to speed 0, and keeps its position as the start of its move.
Sets the next move of one ship of ch5Ships from its last move's end to a place and angles by its order (the tables at 0x8C107B60 and 0x8C107B78), and moves its side effects on a step.

Step 3 of ch5Ships for one ship: on the step's 8th frame (38th for the second in order) it makes a shock ring in the ship's polarity (ch5ShipsRing1). On the 32nd (62nd) it ends it, makes a second one (ch5ShipsRing2) with sequence 0x11, moves the ship's side effects on a step and makes the ship roll faster.

Sets the last move of one ship of ch5Ships that takes part, from where its second move ended: to x -10 for player 1 or 10 for player 2, y -25, z 0, with pitch 0x4000, yaw 0 and a roll angle of -0x20000 (minus two turns) for the first in order or 0x20000 for the second.

The task of ch5Ships, in 6 steps for both ships (ch5ShipsStart, ch5ShipsSlow, ch5ShipsTargetSet, ch5ShipsRings, ch5ShipsFinalSet and ch5ShipsBlend). When its frame count reaches 22 it starts the ships' first move, while they slow down and roll. 51 frames after that move it starts their second move with the rings. 140 frames after the start of that move it puts the camera on the path (mode 0) and eases the camera value at 0x8C1D1510. Then it starts their last move and eases the camera value at 0x8C1D1514, and halfway through the move those at 0x8C1D1508 and 0x8C1D1500. Once the camera is in mode 1 (ch5BossArrivalUpdate), it puts the ships at their places with a turn effect (playerTurnEffect), clears their forced flags and input, sets their speed to 0.5 and their hp to 1, lets players join again and ends.

Makes a task in list 2 that takes both ships through chapter 5's sequence before the boss (ch5ShipsUpdate, ch5ShipsDraw), with the player of the higher score first in a game with two players. It sets the ships' forced flags 0x02, 0x08 and 0x20, clears their shot, switch and release input, stops joining and sets stageEvents 0x0A. Chapter 5's stage program calls it at scroll position 14500.
Draws a ch5EndSpark: its sprite as a quad (spriteDraw3D) at its alpha, from its glow's matrix turned by its angle and moved out by its distance.

The task of a ch5EndSpark: its alpha falls by 51 a frame and it ends below 52. Its distance grows 1.5 times a frame from 0.5 and its size 1.125 and 1.5 times, and it takes a new sprite from 0x11000 to 0x1100F every second frame.

Makes a spark of chapter 5's ending in list 4 (ch5EndSparkUpdate, ch5EndSparkDraw) at a glow matrix of a ship: a random sprite from 0x11000 to 0x1100F at a random angle and size, white or black by the ship's polarity.
Draws a ch5EndLaser's trail of up to 16 points as a strip with texture 0x10C00, white (0x870000) or black (0x840000).

The task of a ch5EndLaser. For 16 frames it turns toward an angle from its start angle, then toward the last fight's object (ch5FinalPosition): in the direction it first picked, faster each frame up to 0x400, and it eases in once it faces it. Within 0x2800 of that direction its speed grows 1.25 times a frame up to 5, else it drops 0.75 times a frame down to 0.25. Within 10 of the object it flashes (effectFollowScaled) and its trail shrinks until it ends. It builds its trail's strip on the stage path.

Makes a homing laser of chapter 5's ending in list 2 (ch5EndLaserUpdate, ch5EndLaserDraw) at a ship's place (ch5EndUpdate passes 0x8 or 0x14 of ch5End), with flags (1 white, 2 black), an angle and a speed, and a trail of 16 points.

Sets the move of one ship of ch5End that takes part, from its position and angles to a place by its order (the first at x -4.5, y -25.5, the second at x 12.5, y -15) with three turns of roll for the first and two the other way for the second. It sets forced flag 0x04 in any case.

Draws a glow of a ship of ch5End while its alpha (0x152) is not 0, white or black by the ship's polarity: sprite 0x10A02 at the glow's scale (0x158) times 0.875 to 1.125 at random, and while 0x164 is not 0, sprite 0x10900 at 5 times the value at 0x164, at the random angle of that ship and glow (0x168 to 0x174).

Draws one ship of ch5End that takes part until it bursts: on the stage path at its place, turned by its roll. It draws the ship's model (shipModelDraw) while the ship's state is below 3 and forced flag 0x04 is set. It keeps two matrices beside the ship (x 1.75 and -1.75) at 0x178 and 0x1B8 (0x80 more for the second ship), each with a glow (ch5EndGlow).
The draw of ch5End: both ships (ch5EndDrawOne).
Makes two charge particles (chargeParticleCreate) into the two glow matrices of a ship of ch5End, at the distance at 0x15C with the shrink at 0x160, which stop when byte 3 is set.

Makes a shock ring (shockRingCreate, 31 segments) that follows a ship's point of ch5End: white or black by the ship's polarity, at scale 2. Its outer radius starts at 8 and grows by 0.6 each frame, its inner radius grows from 0 by 0.603, and its alpha falls from 255 by 3 each frame.
Places a ship's point of ch5End on the stage path at 0x278 (12 more for the second ship).

On frame 1 of ch5End's step 4 (31 for the second in order) it makes two rings of explosions (explosionRing, 17 and 9) and an explosion at a ship's point, with sequence 0x102. On the next frame it stops drawing that ship.

The task of ch5End, in 7 steps. When its frame count reaches 24 it puts the camera on the path (mode 0), eases the camera values at 0x8C1D1508, 0x8C1D150C, 0x8C1D1510 and 0x8C1D1500 over 800 frames, and moves the ships to their places over about 820 frames (ch5EndShipsSet, ch5ShipsBlend) while they slow down. Near the end of that move it starts sequence 0x106, and the ships charge (ch5EndCharge) while their glows grow. 66 frames after the move it makes rings (ch5EndRing) and plays sequence 0x101. For 255 frames each ship then fires a homing laser (ch5EndLaser) every frame, to alternate sides, with sparks (ch5EndSpark) at its glows. Then the screen fades to white (fadeTo) and the ships burst (ch5EndShipBurst). On frame 40 it sets ch5CloseRingRequest for the last fight's closing ring. On frame 68 it clears the enemies (enemiesClear), sets the fade to white and lowers the stage's lock (stageUnlock). After the last fade it removes the tasks up to level 199 of lists 0 to 6 (taskRemoveLevel) and shows ch5EndOverlay.

Makes a task in list 2 with level 0x81 that takes both ships through chapter 5's ending (ch5EndUpdate, ch5EndDraw), with the player of the higher score first in a game with two players. It sets the ships' forced flags 0x02, 0x08 and 0x20 and clears their shot, switch and release input. Chapter 5's stage program calls it after the last fight lowers the stage's lock.
Draws a screenSpriteFade sprite at its alpha (spriteDraw), without the play area's clip on a horizontal screen. Sprites 0x5000A and 0x5000B blink (24 of 32 frames).
The task of a screenSpriteFade sprite: it waits its delay, fades in by 15 a frame, holds for its frames, then fades out by 15 a frame and ends.

Makes a task in list 0 (screenSpriteFadeUpdate, screenSpriteFadeDraw) that shows a sprite at screen point 320 less an offset, 240, from the offset, the sprite's flags, the sprite, the frames to hold and the frames to wait.
Draws chapter 5's tunnel: up to three segments (model 0x80001) 400 apart in z, from the multiple of 400 at the path's z, down to z -16000, and at -16000 its end (model 0x80000) 100 further.
Ends chapter 5's tunnel task at stage part 1.
Makes chapter 5's tunnel, a task in list 0 (ch5TunnelUpdate, ch5TunnelDraw). Chapter 5's stage program calls it at its start.

Draws chapter 5's boss room at z -16510, all of it turned by its three angles: model 0x90000, models 0x90001 and 0x90002 at z -10 turned about y by minus and plus the angle at 0x28, models 0x90003 and 0x90004 at y 135 and at x minus and plus the distance at 0x30, and model 0x90005 at y 225.

The task of chapter 5's boss room (ch5BossRoom), in 8 steps. Past scroll position 16000 it plays sequence 0x103 and turns models 0x90001 and 0x90002 apart, faster each frame up to 32, and at 0x1000 sets them back. In stage part 1, phase 1 (the boss's fight) it eases the camera value at 0x8C1D1518 to 50 and spins the whole room: every 16 frames its turn speed about x rises by 1 up to 64 and that about y steps by 1 between 64 and -64, and every 32 frames that about z steps by 1 between 48 and -48. From phase 2 its angles return toward 0, 0.99 times a frame. At stage part 2 it puts models 0x90003 and 0x90004 at x -55 and 55 and eases the camera value to 50. Past scroll position 25 it plays sequence 0x109, eases the camera value to 60 and closes them, faster each frame. When they meet it plays sequence 0x10A. It ends at scroll position 750.
Makes chapter 5's boss room, a task in list 0 (ch5BossRoomUpdate, ch5BossRoomDraw). Chapter 5's stage program calls it at scroll position 14500.

Draws chapter 5's column at z -16510, turned by its angle: 3 models 0xA0001 in stage part 2, else 5, each 400 above the one before. The first is at the highest 535 plus a multiple of 400 not above the path's height, or at 535 for a height between 135 and 535. At 135 or less it draws nothing.
The task of chapter 5's column (ch5Column). Past scroll position 650, every 8 frames its turn speed moves by 1, swinging between 128 and -128. It turns by that speed each frame.
Makes chapter 5's column, a task in list 0 (ch5ColumnUpdate, ch5ColumnDraw). Chapter 5's stage program calls it at the start of stage part 2.
Loads bank 8 under the name ST_BG00 from the file list at 0x8C1093F4, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 4 under the name ST_OBJ00 from the file list at 0x8C10945C, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads bank 5 under the name ST_OBJ01 from the file list at 0x8C1094C8, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Loads the tutorial's banks 8, 4 and 5 at once (tutBankLoadBg00, tutBankLoadObj00, tutBankLoadObj01). The tutorial's stage program calls it at its start.
Fades the screen to black over 90 frames (fadeSet, fadeTo). The tutorial's stage program calls it before its end.

Sets the tutorial's light (its two angles, color 1, 1, 1 with intensity 1 and ambient 0.25, and for the multi-light models the color of light 1 and three more values 0.3, 0.48 and 0.5), and the fog's color to 128, 180, 205, its depths -100 and -800 (fogTableSet) and the fade's level 0.5, with byte 4 of ninjaFadeLevel at 0, and sets fogFadeOn. The tutorial's stage program calls it at its start.
The draw of a tutDifficulty task: for its frames it shows sprites 0x50900 and 0x50901 (kind 0) or 0x50902 to 0x50904 (kind 1), 12 of each 16 frames, then it ends.
Makes a task in list 5 with only a draw (tutDifficultyDraw) that lasts 240 frames and shows a difficulty's sprites in the first 239, kind 0 at screen point 296, 240 and kind 1 at 280, 240.

Outside the attract mode, shows the difficulty (tutDifficulty) by the difficulty option, or by difficultyChoice while that option is USER SELECT: kind 0 for easy, kind 1 for hard, nothing for normal. The tutorial's stage program calls it.
Stops all sounds (soundStopAll), or in a trial game outside the attract mode only the one-shot sound in slot 7. The tutorial's stage program calls it at its end.

Draws a tutBigCreate enemy, turned by its angles: model 0x40000 at its motion's frame and model 0x40001, both with their second texture list (flag 0x10000) when the enemy is black. It files its hit record when model 0x40000 is in view.

The task of a tutBigCreate enemy: puts its hit points into the gauge (hpGaugeSet) and runs its behaviour (0x8C), which ends it with a non-zero result. It steps its motion, places its muzzle points (0x80, and 0x74 up to 1 to the side at random) and makes a muzzle flash (effectFlash) at 0x80 when byte 0x68 is set. At 0 hit points it is destroyed (enemyDestroyed), with two more explosions while it runs motion 1, plays sound 0x0C and ends.

Makes a large enemy of the tutorial in list 3 (tutBigUpdate, tutBigDraw) from a script record (enemyInit) with 10 hit points, model 0x40000 and a looping motion, and extra bytes of the given size at 0x94. The caller sets its behaviour at 0x8C.
The behaviour of a tutDropper: it falls at 0.25 a frame. In its frames 136, 152 and 168 it fires 3 bullets of its color at a ship at 0.4.
A record function of the tutorial's stage script: makes an enemy with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create) that falls and fires at a ship (tutDropperMove).
The behaviour of a tutSlider: it moves by its x speed each frame.
A record function of the tutorial's stage script: makes an enemy with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create) that moves in x at -0.25 a frame and does not fire (tutSliderMove).
The behaviour of a tutStopper: it falls at 0.45 a frame for 80 frames, slows by 0.01 a frame to a stop, fires 3 bullets of its color at a ship, 16 frames apart, at 0.4, and then stays.
A record function of the tutorial's stage script: makes an enemy with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create) that comes down, stops and fires at a ship (tutStopperMove).

The behaviour of a tutSwooper: its fall slows by 0.004 a frame until it rises, and its outward speed grows by 0.002 a frame. After 60 frames it fires 3 bullets of its color at a ship, 32 frames apart, at 0.4. It ends once it is out of view.
A record function of the tutorial's stage script: makes an enemy with model 0x10003 (enemyModel3Create) that falls at 0.6, curves outward to its side and back up (tutSwooperMove).

The behaviour of a tutBigGunner: it falls at 0.25 a frame. In its frames 64 to 100 it fires 10 bullets (bulletSpriteFireAt10508) of its color along its angle from its muzzle, 4 frames apart, at 0.75, each with a muzzle flash and its motion restarted.
A record function of the tutorial's stage script: makes a large enemy (tutBigCreate) that falls and fires straight (tutBigGunnerMove).

The behaviour of a tutBigAimer, which always faces a ship (aimAtPlayer). It falls at 0.95 a frame, slower by 0.01 each frame, and once it rises it also drifts outward. After 101 frames it slows back to a stop. Then it fires 15 bullets (bulletSpriteFireAt10508) of its color at the ship, 4 frames apart, at 0.75, with muzzle flashes and motion 1, and stays.
A record function of the tutorial's stage script: makes a large enemy (tutBigCreate) that comes down, stops and fires at a ship (tutBigAimerMove).
The behaviour of a tutBigStopper: it falls at 1.75 a frame, slower by 0.04 each frame, until it stops, and then stays.
A record function of the tutorial's stage script: makes a large enemy (tutBigCreate) that comes down and stops without firing (tutBigStopperMove).
Starts the tutorial's stage script at 0x8C1085B8 (scriptStart). The tutorial's stage program calls it at its start.
Draws the tutorial's background: the model list at 0x8C109338 (2 models) three times, 400 apart in z, moved by its scroll.
Moves the tutorial's background's scroll by 1 a frame, wrapping at 400.

Makes the tutorial's background, a task in list 0 (tutBgUpdate, tutBgDraw) whose data is its scroll, a float. The game asks for 0 data bytes, so the float lies in syMalloc's padding. The port's tutBg (port/src/native.cpp) asks for the 4 bytes. The tutorial's stage program calls it at its start through tutBgJump.
Jumps to tutBg (a stub of mov.l and jmp). The tutorial's stage program calls it at its start.
The task of tutUnlockAfter: counts its frames down, and at 0 it lowers the stage's lock (stageUnlock) and ends.
Makes a task in list 3 with no draw (tutUnlockAfterUpdate) that lowers the stage's lock after a number of frames. The tutorial's stage program calls it after each step.
Draws a tutCaption: its sprite and the next one, at its place, fading in over its first 15 frames and out over its last 15, without the play area's clip on a horizontal screen.
The task of a tutCaption: counts its frames and ends after its time.

Makes a caption of the tutorial in list 3 (tutCaptionUpdate, tutCaptionDraw): a sprite (with the next one) for a number of frames. Sprite 0x50300 shows at screen point 320, 5, sprites 0x50602 and 0x50704 at 268, 160, and the others at 268, 80, all 80 lower on a horizontal screen. The tutorial's stage program shows one at each step.
The draw of tutWait's kind 0: counts its frames down while the game is paused, and at 0 it ends the pause (pauseEnd) and the task.

The draw of tutWait's kind 1: sprite 0x50100, moved by the HUD's offset (optionScreenX, optionScreenY), with a size that pulses every 64 frames. Its alpha wraps at a byte, so it ramps between 0 and 255 every 8 frames.
The task of tutWait's kind 1: counts its frames down and ends at 0.

Makes a task in list 3 for a number of frames: kind 0 pauses the game (pauseState 2) until the frames have passed (tutPauseDraw), kind 1 shows a prompt (tutPromptUpdate, tutPromptDraw). The tutorial's stage program calls it.

Draws the tutorial's controller: model 0x50003 with the stick (model 0x50002) tilted by the input, and two buttons, each drawn as model 0x50001 and model 0x50000. A lit button draws its model 0x50000 0.6 lower and shows sprite 0x50200, which blinks every 2 frames while tutPadBlinkOn is set.

Reads player 1's input for the tutorial's controller: up and down tilt the stick by 0x11C7 about x, left and right about z. Holding shot lights the first button, pressing switch lights the second for 20 frames, and pressing release lights both for 20 frames.
Makes the tutorial's controller, a task in list 3 (tutPadUpdate, tutPadDraw) that shows the recorded input. The tutorial's stage program calls it at its start.
Sets tutPadBlinkOn: while it is not 0, the lit buttons of the tutorial's controller blink. The tutorial's stage program sets it to 1 and later to 0.
Draws a string in the ranking's sprite font: letters as sprites from 0x20000 (A), digits from 0x11800 (0), and anything else as a gap. The step after an I is narrower.
Ends the fades of a ranking panel's 21 rows at once: rows that fade in show at full alpha, rows that fade out are hidden.
Moves on the rows of a ranking panel that a sweep (a position and a height) covers: hidden rows start to fade in, shown rows start to fade out.
Fades the 21 rows of a ranking panel: a row that appears gains alpha and glow by up to 18 a frame, then loses the glow by up to 24 a frame. A row that goes loses alpha by up to 18 a frame.

The draw of the ranking scene (sceneRankingStart). While it waits for input after a game or VIEW RANKING, it blinks the difficulties for left and right (textPrintf). Each panel has a header row with RANKING (rankingTextDraw), the difficulty, the list's name and sprites 0x20100 to 0x20103, then 20 entries (rankings) at their alpha and glow: the place, the score (with the chain in the chapter lists), the chapter (lists 0 and 6), the name and the date. Outside the attract demo, a held trigger replaces the name and date with the mode, stock and extend.

Draws the play data after a game at the task's alpha: PLAY DATA for 1-PLAYER or 2-PLAYERS, the DIFFICULTY, the EXTEND and the PLAYER STOCK, the TOTAL SCORE, and each chapter's score and longest chain (chapterScores). With one player these are of the last player to join (playerLastJoined). With two players the scores are of both (chapterScoresTotal) and the chains of each. It blinks You're Real DOT-EATER! when the two counts of playerNoShotChapters add up to 5 with one player, or DOT-EATERS! when both are 5 with two.
The task of rankingPlayData: waits for a button (mask 0x3070F) on either pad, then fades out by 15 a frame and ends.
Makes the play data screen, a task in list 0 (rankingPlayDataUpdate, rankingPlayDataDraw). rankingUpdate makes it after a game.

The task of the ranking scene (sceneRankingStart), in 6 steps. It starts sequence 0x3E, and after a game it first shows the play data (rankingPlayData) until a button is pressed. Then it shows list 0, or list 6 after a game with two players, at the game's difficulty: the rows sweep in (rankingRowsSweep, rankingRowsFade) with sequence 0x3C. When it comes from the attract demo the panels take turns, each list for 300 frames, and after list 11 it fades out. Else up picks the previous list and down, A or C the next (0 to 11, wrapping), left and right the difficulty, each with sequence 0x3D, and B fades out with sound 1. After the fade it stops all sounds and requests the logos (scene 2) while gameDemo is set, as after a game or the attract demo, else the title (scene 4), as after VIEW RANKING.
Loads bank 2 under the name RANKING from the file list at 0x8C109A3C, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).
Draws the ranking's background: model 0x20000 at its motion's frame, with the camera at 0x8C109A1C, a quarter turn about z on a horizontal screen and without the play area's clip.
Steps the motion of the ranking's background (model 0x20000) by 1 frame, wrapping.

Sets the ranking's light (angles 0xF380 and 0xC000, color 1, 1, 1 with intensity 1 and ambient 0.5, and for the multi-light models light 1 at 1, 1, 1 and three more values of 0.5), and a black fog with depths -200 and -1200 (fogTableSet) and the fade's level 0.6, with byte 4 of ninjaFadeLevel at 0, and sets fogFadeOn.
Sets the ranking's light and fog (rankingLightFog) and makes its background, a task in list 0 (rankingBgUpdate, rankingBgDraw). sceneRankingStart calls it.
Draws a string in the ending's sprite font, as rankingTextDraw does: letters from sprite 0x20000, digits from 0x11800, and a narrower step after an I.
The draw of the trial game's ending: sprite 0x20200.

The task of the trial game's ending (sceneEndingStart). After the fade in it shows its sprite for 2100 frames, or until a player in the game presses a button, and fades to black over 90 frames. After the fade it clears the joined players, adds the play time (playTimeAdd) and goes on as endingFinish does, with chapterScoresTotal after a game with two players.

Draws the lines of the staff roll from its current line on, each after the last by its height: a text (textDraw), a text in the ending's font (endingTextDraw, flag 0x02) or a sprite (kind 1). Lines fade in and out over 16 at the ends of the screen, at y 240 and -240.

Clears the joined players and adds the play time (playTimeAdd). After a practice it requests the title (scene 4). Else it sets soundOff to 1 and calls gameDemoSet, which sets the attract mode and soundOff back to 0. Then it asks for a save and requests the ranking (scene 3) with the play data first.

The task of the staff roll (sceneEndingStart). After the fade in it scrolls the lines at 0x8C109AF8 from y 320 by 0.5 a frame, and drops each line once it is past -256. At the roll's end mark it fades the music and the screen out over 90 frames. A button press of a player in the game, outside the name entry, does the same at once. After the fade it calls endingFinish.
Loads bank 2 under the name ENDING from the file list at 0x8C10A498, at once with 0 or else over frames (bankLoadMode).

Draws the ending's background outside a trial game: models 0x20000 and 0x20001 (at its motion's frame) under the camera motion at 0x8C10A48C at its frame (njCameraMotion), without the play area's clip.
Outside a trial game, steps the frame of the ending's camera motion by 1, wrapping at its 2401 frames, and the motion of model 0x20001.
Sets the ending's light: angles 0xF380 and 0xC000, color 1, 1, 1 with intensity 1 and ambient 0.5, and for the multi-light models light 1 at 1, 1, 1 and three more values of 0.5.
Sets the ending's light (endingLight), makes its background, a task in list 0 (endingBgUpdate, endingBgDraw), and sets DAT_8c10a1a8. sceneEndingStart calls it.

The game's main loop: sets Ninja and the game up (gameInit), then runs one frame at a time (pdExecPeripheralServer, gameFrame, the vertical blank). It stops when gameExitRequest is set and no card save runs (saveIdle), and it sets gameExitRequest when gameFrame returns nonzero or the disc tray opens. Then it calls gameRelease and frees Ninja's buffers.
Sets the game up before the first frame. frameCount counts from here.
Frees gamePads, removes every task of the 7 lists, stops the loads (loadsAbort), frees the 16 graphics banks and the 4 sound banks and closes the sound. gameMain calls it after the main loop.
Changes to a scene: removes every task, saves to the card when saveRequest and optionAutosave are set, makes the scene current and calls its start function, whose result is the next request.
Runs a frame of the scene: checks the soft reset, runs the task lists 0 to 5 (only 6 while paused), opens the frame, draws the lists and renders.

Copies a controller's state into the game's own copy (gamePads), with the directions turned a quarter turn (up to left, down to right, left to down, right to up) when optionRotateButtons is set. While idleDarken is set, a press resets the idle count idleFrames, and while the screen is darkened (idleDarkened) the copy is all zeros and a press ends the darkening.

One frame of the game: reads both controllers (gameReadPad), updates the VMU screens, then runs the scene (gameTaskFrame) or changes to the requested one (gameEnterScene), and adds 1 to frameCount. While idleDarken is set, more than 10800 frames without a press start to darken the screen step by step. See docs/game.md, The frame.
Empties the 7 task lists.
Makes a task with `size` bytes of data at the end of a task list, with an update and a draw function. Returns the data's address, after the task's 0x18-byte header (Task).
Calls the update function of each living task of a list, and removes the tasks whose removal countdown ends.
Calls the draw function of each living task of a list.
Calls a task's removal function, unlinks the task from its list and frees it. Returns the next task.
Marks the living tasks of a list up to a level for removal, which taskRunList does when it next reaches them.
Removes the tasks of a list up to a level at once.
Marks the living tasks of a list that have this update function for removal, which taskRunList does when it next reaches them.

Scene 1: loads the common data (COMDAT) and the notice (WARNDAT_DC). Its task shows the notice, reads the save from the VMU or writes a new one when the card has room, waits for Start and then requests scene 2.
Scene 2: the logos.

Scene 3: the ranking lists (RANKING bank), after a game first the play data. After VIEW RANKING or the attract demo it clears gameTwoPlayers and sets difficulty from optionDifficulty, with NORMAL for USER SELECT, or demoCount mod 3 in the attract demo.
Scene 4: the title and its menus (titleTask).
Scene 5: the mode select after GAME START.
Scene 6, chapter 1: loads the chapter's sound banks, sets the fade and sceneNext, and starts the stage with the chapter's stage program.
Scene 7, chapter 2: loads the chapter's sound banks, sets the fade and sceneNext, and starts the stage. In a trial game the ending follows this chapter.
Scene 8, chapter 3: loads the chapter's sound banks, sets the fade and sceneNext, and starts the stage with the chapter's stage program.
Scene 9, chapter 4: loads the chapter's sound banks, sets the fade and sceneNext, and starts the stage with the chapter's stage program.
Scene 10, chapter 5: loads the chapter's sound banks, loads bank 5 at once (ch5BankLoadObj03), sets the fade and sceneNext (12, the ending) and starts the stage with the chapter's stage program.

Scene 11: the tutorial, a stage that always plays recorded input (demoStart). It starts sequence 0x10B and keeps both players from joining (joinLocked). Its sceneNext is scene 3 in the attract demo, chapter 1 in a trial game and the title else.

Scene 12: the ending (ENDING bank, endingBg). Unless gameNoRanking is set, it starts the name entry (nameEntryStart) of each player in the game for whom rankingFindPlaces finds a place. A trial game then shows endingTrialUpdate with a fade in from black, else the staff roll (endingRollUpdate) with a fade in from white, each over 120 frames. Sets gameClearFlags.

Starts the stage of a chapter or of the tutorial with its stage program: makes the stage's task (stageUpdate, stageDraw), runs the program's first commands, and makes the camera, the ships (playerCreate), the HUDs and the HP gauge. It also empties the script groups, clears bossTimeLeft and the 20 bytes from stageLocks.
Reads a whole file from the disc into a block from syMalloc. Gives the file's size.

Loads a file's list of sound banks into a slot of soundBankLists and sends each bank to the sound driver, unless the slot already holds the list of that name. soundInit loads the default list into slot 0, and other scenes load theirs into slot 1.
Gives the fade one color.
Makes a task that changes the fade's four corners to these ARGB colors in a number of frames.

Draws the fade's quad (fadeQuad, the whole screen) while its first corner's alpha is not 0, with the blending flags in fadeBlend (spriteMode). With screenHorizontal set it turns the clipping off first, unless fadeTurned is set: then it draws the quad turned by polygonTurn instead.

Makes a player's ship at a stage's start (stageStart): a task in list 2 whose data is a Player, kept in players. The ship takes its polarity from playerPolarity, and starts out of the game (state 4) when its player is not in the game, in play (state 2) in chapter 1 at stagePart 0, else with a new life (state 0).

The update of the ship's task, by its state: 0 sets up a new life, 1 flies the ship in, 1 and 2 move the ship (playerMove) until a hit or the scenery ends the life, 3 waits 60 frames and then starts the next life or puts the player out (playerOut), and 4 and 5 do nothing. The first player's task also reads the demo's input (demoInputRead). See docs/game.md, The player.

Draws the ship, which files its hit records (shipModelDraw), unless it is hidden. When the player of a ship out of the game (state 4) has joined, the ship starts a new life (state 0), after a wait in state 5 while the player's bit in playersOut or joinLocked is set. In chapter 1 at stagePart 0 and stagePhase 1 it goes to play (state 2) at once.
Steers the ship within its bounds, and runs the turn of a polarity switch: 14 frames, the color changing halfway.

Turns a player's pad into playerInput: the directions, and shot, switch and release by the player's chosen buttons (buttonShot, buttonSwitch, buttonRelease). With buttonShotSwitch set, shot and switch pressed together count as a release. playerMove calls it only when no recorded input plays (demoInput).
Clears a player's input and the ship's held and pressed buttons.
Shoots, releases the homing lasers and starts a polarity switch from a player's input.

Sets the hit attributes of the ship (0x60 for polarity 0, 0x50 for 1) and of its field (1 or 2, with 0x08 for the second player) by its polarity. It keeps the polarity in playerPolarity, which playerCreate gives the ship at the next stage's start.
Puts the ship at its start for a new life.

Makes a sprite at a ship in the color of the ship's polarity at that time, a task in list 2 (turnEffectUpdate, turnEffectDraw). It follows the ship and fades out when the ship's next turn starts (flag 0x20), or ends at once when flag 0x04 is in the ship's flags or forced. playerMove makes it when a turn switches the polarity, and playerUpdate when a new life starts.
Takes `amount` from a player's playerEnergy, down to 0. playerButtons takes 10 for each homing laser of a release, and playerShotCreate takes 2 for a shot and 1 for a side shot in the prototype mode.
Fires a shot from the ship, a task in list 2. In the prototype mode a shot costs 2 energy and a side shot 1, and a shot without the energy ends after a few frames.
Makes a homing laser of a release, which picks its target with laserTarget.
Starts a MIDI sequence by its id: the slot of the bank list in the high byte and the entry in the low byte. With a position, it gets a pan and a volume.
Starts a stage script, an array of ScriptRecords, in a task of list 3.
The task of a stage script: takes its current record through scriptStep each frame.

Checks a stage script's current record and returns how many records to move on. When a run condition holds (scroll position, frames on the record, frames of the script, empty group) it calls the record's function, adds the result to a group with flag 0x800 (scriptGroupAdd) and returns next. When a branch condition holds it returns branch without the call, else 0. See docs/game.md, The stage scripts.
Adds what a script record made to one of the 4 script groups.
Removes a member from a script group and closes the gap.
Runs each frame and drops the group members whose task is marked for removal, so that a record can wait for an empty group.
Empties the 4 script groups and starts the task of scriptGroupsUpdate in list 3, at each stageStart.
Returns the number of members in a script group.
Ends the task whose data it gets: marks it for removal, so it is no longer updated or drawn and taskRunList removes it when it next reaches it.
Adds points to a player's score, and gives a life at extendScore.

Counts a kill of color 1 or 2 for the chain of the player who made it, in chainSet. Three kills of one color in a row complete a set: chain grows by 1, chainMax follows it and chainBonus pays. A kill of the other color before a set is complete sets chain to 0 and starts a new set.
Draws the label of a chain bonus (chainBonus). Its first call puts the label where the kill was on the screen, within the screen's edges. Then it draws the chain's step, or MAX, and the points.

The task of a chain bonus's label (chainBonus), once chainBonusLabelDraw has placed it: moves the label by 0.5 a frame, lowers its flash by 16 a frame, and shrinks the MAX label by 0.025 a frame down to 0.825. Once its frame counter passes 32, it lowers the label's alpha by 32 a frame and ends when the alpha is 32 or less.

Pays the bonus of a step in a chain of kills of one color: 100 points at the first step, doubled at each step, up to 25,600 at the ninth and every later one (MAX). Shows the points where the kill was, in a task of chainBonusLabelUpdate and chainBonusLabelDraw.
Fills a hit record: its attribute, hit points, power and its two shapes.
hitInit, and registers the object in hitSlots so that homing lasers can aim at it.
Finds the sphere around all spheres of a hit shape.
Registers an object in a free slot of hitSlots, which homing lasers aim at. Returns the slot.

Fills an enemy's common part from its script record's data: the position, the angles, the color from the data's byte 0x38 and the hit record. With the first argument 0, homing lasers can aim at the enemy (hitRegister).
Fills an enemy's common part (enemyInitCommon), for an enemy that homing lasers can aim at.
Adds an enemy's velocity to its position.

Called by an enemy whose hit points reached 0: counts the kill for the chain of the player who hit it this frame (chainCount, hitBy bit 0x08 picks player 2). Then it makes the enemy's explosion (enemyExplosion) and its bullets (enemyDeathBullets). It clears the explosion's flag 0x40 when that player's chainSet count stands at 2.

Takes the hitter's power, doubled when their colors (attribute & 3) differ, from the target's hit points unless the target has flag 0x02 or 0x04. A hitter with flag 0x01 scores 10 points for each point of damage unless the target has flag 0x04 or 0x08. It also marks the hit in the hitBy bits and, for a hitter with flag 0x40, requests the hit sound (hitSoundRequest).
Tests each record of one hit list against each of another and applies the hits.

Returns 1 when the hitter's shape 0 and the target's shape 1 both have bounding spheres. Otherwise it tests the hitter's bounding sphere, or its first sphere, against the target's bounding sphere, or its first sphere (njCollisionCheckSS).

Files a hit record with hit points left in one of the 5 hit lists, with its two shapes placed by the current matrix (hitShapePlace). A record with no shape placed is not filed and gets its hitBy cleared. For a record with a laser slot, it also sets the slot's position, record and in-view mark.

Places a hit shape's spheres by the current matrix into the sphere buffer (hitShapeTransform), with a bounding sphere in out[0] when the shape has more than one. Returns 0 when there is no shape, or when it is out of view (sphereInView) unless flag 0x100 is set.

Writes each sphere of a hit shape, placed by the current matrix, to the next places of the sphere buffer, and stores the first one's address in out[1]. A kind 0 entry becomes a sphere at the matrix's origin with its radius times 0.0001.
Empties the 5 hit lists and their sphere buffers, for the next frame.
Clears the hitBy byte of each record filed in the 5 hit lists. hitPass calls it before it tests the lists.
Tests the hit lists against each other: the shots against the enemies, the fields against the bullets, the bullets against the ships and the enemies against the ships.

Stores a hit sound to play at a position with a priority from 1 to 3. A request replaces a pending one of a lower priority, and one of priority 3 replaces any. hitPass plays the pending sound and then waits 4 frames before the next.
Sets the hit system up for a stage: the tasks that test the hit lists and clear them for the next frame, the scenery and the laser slots.
Frees the 200 slots that homing lasers aim at, and makes their task.
The task of the laser slots: clears each slot's in-view mark for the next frame, and frees a slot one frame after its object's removal starts.
Whether a slot holds an object that a homing laser may aim at: used, in view and not flagged 0x80.
Returns the address of a slot's position, which hitFile sets to the center of the first sphere of the object's shape 1 at each filing.
Counts a laser's damage on its way to a slot's object: 10, or 20 against the other color.
Takes back a laser's damage from a slot's object: 10, or 20 against the other color.

Picks a target slot for a homing laser at a point: the nearest one in x and y that hitSlotTargetable would accept and whose aimed damage is below its hit points, else the nearest such slot at all. Returns 0xff when there is none. No caller sets wide, which would halve dx and quadruple a positive dy.
Whether a point lies inside the scenery's polygons. A shot stops there, and a ship that is not invulnerable dies.

The update of a shot's task: moves the shot by its y speed and ends it outside x -30 to 30 and y -40 to 40, or with a burst (effectBurst) when stageEvents has 0x08. It marks the shot when it meets the scenery (sceneryHit), and playerShotDraw then ends it.
Draws a shot and files its hit record in hit list 2.

A homing laser's task: it turns toward its target slot and takes a new target from laserTarget when the old one is lost, and for its first 12 frames it also moves with the ship. It stops when its draw saw a hit, when it leaves x -30 to 30, y -40 to 40 without a target, or at stageEvents flag 0x08. Its trail then shrinks and fades until taskEnd.

Draws a homing laser's trail. While the laser flies and has a target, it files the laser's hit record in hit list 2. A record whose hitBy has flag 0x80 (a hit) switches the laser to its ending state 1.
Makes a bullet: a task in list 4 whose data is a Bullet, with a color (0x11 white, 0x22 black), a position and a velocity.
Fires a bullet at an angle with a speed (vectorFromAngle, bulletCreate).
Fires a bullet of a color from a position at an angle with a speed, with sprite 0x10300 (bulletFireAt).

A bullet's task: moves the bullet by its velocity and steps its sprite through 4 frames, one step every second frame. It ends the bullet outside x -30 to 30 and y -40 to 40 widened by its margin, through bulletAbsorbed when its hit points are 0, and with bulletVanish when it lies in the scenery (sceneryHit), its hit record shows a hit, or stageEvents has 0x02.
Draws a bullet and files its hit record in hit list 4. White and black bullets swap their depths from frame to frame.
A field absorbed a bullet (bulletAbsorb).

Makes the spark of an absorbed bullet (absorbSparkUpdate, absorbSparkDraw), which flies from the bullet to the ship of the player that absorbed it (hitBy bit 0x08 picks player 2). Then it gives that player the energy (playerAbsorb).

Makes the effect of a vanishing bullet: an effectBurst (7 for a white bullet, 4 for a black one) at the bullet's position with half its velocity. The bullets' tasks call it before they end a bullet that lies in the scenery, whose hit record shows a hit, or while stageEvents has 0x02.

Gives a player `energy` points of energy, up to 120, and 100 points of score for each (bulletAbsorb calls it for an absorbed bullet). In the prototype mode it gives three times as much energy, up to 999. While finalFight is set it gives only the score, and it calls absorbGlowCreate when the old energy's last digit plus `energy` reaches 10.
The index of the ship nearer to a point: 0 for player 1, 1 for player 2.
The ship nearer to a point.

Returns the angle from a point to a ship: with 0 player 1's and with 1 player 2's, or the other one when that player is not in the game (playersInGame). With 2 it takes the nearer ship when both or neither play, else the one that plays.
Turns an angle and a speed into a velocity. Angle 0 points up.

Called each frame by gameTaskFrame. Unpaused, Start (0x8) on a pad pauses the game unless the player's bit in pauseLocked is set, and sets pausePlayer to 1 or 2. Paused, it stops the vibration and pauses the sound once (not in scene 11), and when pauseEnd is set it resumes the sound and ends the pause.
Stops the vibration units at ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 (pdVibMxStop). pauseUpdate calls it at a pause and gameTaskFrame at a soft reset.
Marks the playing sequences to pause, for the game's pause.
Clears the sequences' pause marks, so that they continue.
Marks the playing and waiting one-shot sounds for the game's pause (pauseUpdate), so that soundServer silences them.
Clears the one-shot sounds' pause marks, so that soundServer gives the silenced ones their level back.

The stage's task: clears stageEvents, moves scrollSpeed toward scrollTarget by scrollStep, adds it to scrollPosition up to the path's end, runs the stage program (stageProgramRun) and sets sceneCamera from the path. Outside the tutorial it pauses the game when both ships are out and no game over runs, and in the attract demo it fades out at frame 3810 and changes to scene 3 at frame 3900.

Starts recorded play, at the start of chapter 1 or 2 in the attract demo and of the tutorial: sets difficulty, gameLives and the first player's lives, seeds the random numbers (randomSeed), sets updateFrames, points demoInput at the recorded input and sets demoInputLeft to its length.
Runs the stage program's commands (stageCommands) until one waits for the next frame. See docs/game.md, The stage program.

Makes a task (easeFloatUpdate) that moves the float at `target` from its value at the start to `value` in `frames` frames on a cosine curve. With a `lock`, the task waits until the lock is 0 and holds it until it ends, so tasks on one lock run one after the other. Stage command 20 (stageCmdEaseFloat) uses it.

The task of easeFloat. With a lock, it first waits until the lock is 0 and takes it. Then it moves the float one frame along the curve each frame, and at the end it sets the float to the value, frees the lock unless flag 0x80 leaves that to easeFloatEnd, and ends.

Makes a task (easeWordTask) that moves the word at `target` from its value at the start to `value` in `frames` frames on a cosine curve. With a `lock`, the task waits until the lock is 0 and holds it until it ends, so tasks on one lock run one after the other. Stage command 24 (stageCmdEaseWord) uses it.
Slows the scroll down so that it stops at a position (stage command 26).
Stage command 0: stops the stage program.
Stage command 1: loads the camera's path (pathCreate).
Stage command 2: raises the first byte of stageLocks.
Stage command 3: waits until the first byte of stageLocks is 0, then raises stagePhase.
Stage command 4: waits until the lock that it names is 0.
Stage command 5: waits until scrollPosition reaches its position.
Stage command 6: raises stagePart and sets stagePhase to 0.

Stage command 7: ends the stage and sets stagePart to 0. Outside the practice mode it changes to sceneNext, after playersRestore in scene 11. In the practice mode it adds the play time (playTimeAdd), stops the sound, clears playersInGame and changes to scene 4, the title.
Stage command 8: calls a function with the stage's data.
Stage command 9: calls a function with one of the command's words.
Stage command 10: calls a function with two of the command's words.
Stage command 11: calls a function with three of the command's words.
Stage command 12: calls a function with four of the command's words.
Stage command 13: as command 8, once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 14: as command 9, once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 15: as command 10, once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 16: as command 11, once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 17: as command 12, once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 18: sets a float.
Stage command 19: sets a float once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 20: moves a float to a value over a number of frames (easeFloat).
Stage command 21: as command 20, once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 22: sets a word.
Stage command 23: sets a word once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 24: moves a word to a value over a number of frames (easeWord).
Stage command 25: as command 24, once the scroll reaches its position.
Stage command 26: slows the scroll down to stop at a position (scrollStopAt).

Builds a path from an array of PathPoint (flags, position, three angles and a value) whose last point has flag 0x80: the distance along it at each point and the tables for its straight and curved segments (pathSlopes, pathCurves). stageCmdPath makes the stage's path with it.
Frees a path (pathCreate) and its distance and slope tables.

Returns a path's position, three angles and value at a distance along it, each on a straight line or, when the segment's first point has that value's flag bit (0x1 to 0x40), on a cubic curve. Each of the three outputs may be 0.
Starts a one-shot sound by its id, as soundPlay does for sequences.
Takes a one-shot player's slot for a sound id (soundSlotFind) and sets the sound to start.
Takes a sequence player's slot for a sound id (soundSlotFind) and sets the sound to start.

Returns a free slot in the range that a sound's entry gives. Else it takes the slot with the smallest priority number below the sound's (0 counts as 16), the oldest of those, then the oldest one of the same priority, then one that holds the same id, then the paused slot with the smallest priority number, or returns -1.
A sound's pan from the x of its position.
Returns a sound's level: its volume plus 0.4 times the size of its position's x, within -127 to 127. In mono it returns the volume.

Runs each frame for the 8 sequence and the 20 one-shot slots: starts the sounds that wait with their level, frees the slots whose sounds the library reports done, and counts their age. It pauses and continues the marked sequences, and silences the marked one-shot sounds and gives them their level back.
Stops every sequence: lets paused ones continue, clears the slots, and stops all in the library.
Opens the sound library's 8 sequence players and 20 one-shot players, and loads SFX_DEFAULT.BIN into slot 0 of soundBankLists.

Fires bullets of a destroyed enemy's color at the player who made the kill: none on easy, on normal only after a kill of the enemy's own color, and on hard always, fewer and slower after a kill of the other color.

Makes an enemy's explosion (effectExplosion) with a random angle and turn and a scale within 5 percent of the given one. Then it makes bursts of 8 particles each (effectParticles) at angles spread around 0x8000, 4 bursts when flag 0x40 is set and the low bits are not 1, else 2, and 4 more particles in any direction.
Makes an explosion: a task of explosionUpdate and explosionDraw.
Makes a number of particles (effectParticle) with sprite 0x10a02 at a position, at angles spread by a mask around a base angle, and with random speeds and scales around given values.
Makes a Particle, which flies, slows and shrinks until it is gone or off the screen.
Makes an EffectSprite at a position with a velocity, a scale, a depth and a random angle, which flies and grows (burstUpdate). The flag 0x80 picks effectSpriteDrawDepth, and else effectSpriteDraw.

Makes a flash, such as a ship's muzzle flash (flashUpdate, flashDraw): one of four short animations by kind bits 0 and 1, with sprite flags, a scale (1 when none), an angle and an optional owner task whose position it follows. Kind bit 0x80 gives the depth value 1.0001 instead of 1.001.
Seeds the random numbers (randomState).
Returns the next random number: randomState becomes ((4s + 2) * (4s + 3)) >> 2 in 32 bits, with s the state before.
A random float from -1 to 1.
The C library's atan2 with its error codes.
Makes the gauge of hit points at each stageStart.
Draws the gauge of hit points, unless a demo plays.
Puts the hit points of the object hit this frame (gaugeSlot) into the gauge.
Writes the default options. It also sets chapterReached to 1, playTime to 0, playTimeNextCredit to 3600, creditsPerGame to 3 and gameClearFlags to 0.
Writes the default rankings: 100,000 points minus 1,000 for each place, TRE, September 5, 2002.
Writes the default save block: the options and the rankings.
The sum of the save block's bytes after the identifier and the sum, which saveSum holds.
Makes the card file's image in saveImage from saveHeader and the save block.
Frees saveImage when it is set, and sets it to 0.

Starts to write the save block to the card (buSaveFile) and returns 1, or -1 when that fails. saveWriteDone takes the result. Without `force`, it writes nothing and returns 0 when saveCalcSum is the same as saveSum.
Takes the result of a save when the card is ready again.
Starts to read the card file into saveImage.
Takes the result of a load: copies the block from the image when its identifier matches.

Gives the game the options of the save block: difficulty (difficultyChoice when optionDifficulty is 3), lives, extend and the screen. When saveCheck fails, it first writes the defaults (saveReset) and returns -1. It also sets stereo or mono from the console's sound setting (syCfgGetSoundMode).

Adds the game's time to playTime in seconds (gameFrames / 60), once per game, when the game ends. When playTime reaches playTimeNextCredit, creditsPerGame grows by 1 and the next credit comes 3600 seconds later, and the step after 9 credits gives free play (0xFF). It sets gameClearFlags 0x2, 0x1, 0x4 and 0x8 at 5, 10, 15 and 20 hours, and returns 1 when the credits or the flags changed.

Puts this game's scores into the rankings of the difficulty at the places in rankPlaces, with the name, the date and the game's settings, and moves the lower entries down. With one player these are the player's total and chapter scores, with two players their added scores in lists 6 to 11. nameEntryFinish calls it at the end of the name entry.
Whether a point, taken relative to an origin, lies inside a polygon of the scenery: within its bounds and on the inner side of each edge. A polygon with flag 0x01 gives the inverse result.
The current matrix's position, turned for a vertical screen.
A point that the current matrix transforms, turned for a vertical screen.
Whether a sphere (x, y, z, radius) reaches the plane z = -depth of sceneCamera, with x within 27.5 and y within 37.5 of 0, each widened by the radius.
While fogFadeOn is set, turns Ninja's fog on or off for the next draws by bit 30 (0x40000000) of a sprite's or model's flags, or Ninja's fade instead when the mode at ninjaFadeLevel + 4 is 1.

Sets the draw mode from a sprite's flags: point sampling with bit 26 (0x4000000) and bilinear filtering without it, the fog (drawFog), and the blending by bits 24 and 25 (0 alpha blending, 1 additive, 2 the sprite's color times the inverse of the color behind, 3 unchanged).

Sets the texture of a sprite id, which holds the bank in bits 16 to 31, the sprite set in bits 8 to 15 and the sprite in bits 0 to 7. It selects the bank's texture list and the set's texture, plus flag bits 16 to 21 when flag bit 23 (0x800000) is set. Returns the address of the sprite's four corners (NJS_TEXTURE_VTX).
Draws a sprite at a screen position and angle. The id gives the bank, the sprite and the frame, and the flags the blending, the filter and the vertex builder.
Draws a sprite at the current matrix's position, projected to the screen.
Draws a sprite at the current matrix's position, projected to the screen, with the offset added to the position's z for the sprite's depth only (1/-(z + offset)).
Draws a sprite at the current matrix's position, projected to the screen, with the given depth value for its corners in place of 1/-z.

Sets the draw of a model up from its draw flags: the texture list, the fog (drawFog), lightOff without bit 14 (0x4000) and the bits of njControl3D. With bit 27 (0x8000000) and without bit 31 it sets nothing and returns 0x3f when njCnkModelClip finds the model outside the view. Else it returns 0.

Draws model id & 0xffff of bank id >> 16: sets it up (modelSetup) and draws it with the chunk draw function that flags & 0xf picks from the table at 0x8C0CFA80. Flag bit 16 picks the model's second texture list. Returns 0x3f when modelSetup leaves the model out, else 0.
Returns 0 when the save block's identifier (saveId) is the game's, else -1. optionsApply calls it and writes the defaults (saveReset) on -1.
Copies a string with its end.
Sets the sound to stereo: soundStereo, the library's pan mode and volumes, and the console's setting.
Sets the sound to mono: soundStereo, the library's pan mode and volumes, and the console's setting.
Puts a player into the game: sets the player's bit in playersInGame, clears the scores, and gives the lives and the first extend. The score starts at the player's continues, up to 9.
A player joins: playerStart, and the buttons from the options.
Clears a player's score and the scores for the ranking lists.
Opens the disc's directories (fileDirs).
Changes to a directory of fileDirs.
Clears one of the 16 graphics banks.
Opens the disc's directories and clears the 16 graphics banks.
Starts to read a file from the disc, one file at a time.
Returns 0 when the read of fileReadStart is done, a positive value while it runs and -1 on an error or when no read is open.
Ends a disc read and closes the file.

Reads the chunk at an offset of a Ninja file in memory: copies its data into a new block from syMalloc and adds the block's address to the pointers that the POF0 chunk after it lists. Advances the offset, gives the chunk's tag and returns the block. Returns 0 with the tag 0x2a2a2a2a at a tag it does not know.

Loads a model file of a bank's list in steps: keeps the model (NJCM), the texture list (NJTL) and the motions (NMDM), then loads the textures, from a PVM file when the entry names one. With byte 0 of the request set it reads the disc in the background (fileReadStart), else at once (fileLoad). Returns 1 until it is done, then 0, and -1 on an error with an error text at +0x20 of the request.
Adds a polygon of a stage object to the scenery that ships and shots collide with. Room for 128, not checked.
Empties the scenery's polygons, at each frame.
Whether a screen position lies outside the screen and a margin: x from -320 to 960, y from -240 to 800.
Whether the current matrix's position lies off the screen (offScreen).
Whether a point that the current matrix transforms lies off the screen.

Maps a point through the current matrix to the screen (pointOffScreen) and from there to the play plane, in the units of the enemies' positions. On the vertical screen the screen's edges give 30 and -30 in x and 40 and -40 in y, and the horizontal screen uses Ninja's screen centre and scale.
Starts an Animation: a list of sprites and the frames to show each.
Moves an Animation on by a frame. Gives 1 at the list's end.

The task of an explosion (effectExplosion): moves it by its velocity, multiplies the velocity by its drag factor and turns its sprites. After its first frames it steps its Animation and grows by 1.005 each frame, and from frame 20 it fades by 10 each frame until it ends. With flag 0x80 a second, tinted sprite fades in meanwhile and fades out before the end.

Draws an explosion (effectExplosion) at its position: sprite 0x10900 at a size from a table in its first frames, then the current sprite of its Animation, with its alpha and angle. While byte 5 is not 0 it also draws the Animation's sprite at 0.75 of the size, in the color of bytes 5 to 7.

The task of a particle: shrinks it by its shrink value, moves it by its velocity and slows the velocity to 0.95 each frame. It ends the particle when its scale is no longer above the shrink value. particleDraw ends it off the screen.
Draws a particle's sprite at its position, and ends the particle when it is off the screen (matrixOffScreen).

Makes an EffectSprite at a position with a scale, an angle and a depth (followUpdate). With an owner task it keeps copying that position and ends when the owner's removal starts. The flag 0x40 picks effectSpriteDrawPlain, 0x80 effectSpriteDrawDepth, and else effectSpriteDraw.
The task of a following EffectSprite: moves it with its task, steps its animation and fades it out after the end.

The task of effectBurst's EffectSprite: steps its animation, moves it by its velocity and grows its scale by 1.05 at each frame. After the animation's end it loses 0x40 of alpha at each frame and ends at 0x40 or less.
Draws an EffectSprite's current sprite (its Animation's id) at its position, with its alpha, flags, scale, depth and angle.
