Draws an EffectSprite at its position, with the camera's depth taken from its z, and with its depth field as the sprite's depth value (spriteAtMatrixDepth). effectFollow and effectBurst pick it for the flag 0x80.

Draws an EffectSprite at its position without the camera's depth, with the sprite's depth from that position (spriteAtMatrix). It does not use the depth field. effectFollow picks it for the flag 0x40.

Draws a text at a screen position, one quad for each character from a font texture that holds a grid of 16 by 8 characters from the space on. Each character takes its width from the font's table (textWidth). Flag bits 8 and 9 align the text along its width and bits 10 and 11 along its height (0 start, 1 middle, 2 end).
Returns a text's width: the sum of its characters' widths from the font's table (0.5, 0.75 or 1) times 16.
Prints a formatted text at x and y, as sprintf does, with the font's sprites. It prints the boot screen's text.

Makes a lens flare task: a light sprite in the direction of its two angles, seen from the camera, and 10 flare sprites. The first callback runs once at the start and the second at each frame, before the task places the light. Chapter 1 makes two: through ch1Flare1 from ch1IntroUpdate, and through ch1Flare2 from its stage program (ch1BossArea).

Draws the disc error screen: two lines that say that the disc could not be read and that the console must be restarted, and `message`, which names the error. It draws it again every 5 vertical blanks until the disc tray opens, then calls syBtExit.
With screenHorizontal set, clips the draws to the play area, the 32-pixel tiles 4 to 15 across and 0 to 14 down. Without it, turns the clipping off.
Turns the clipping off for the whole screen.
Sets the clipping and the aspect for the play area.
Runs the picture on the VMU's screen in a controller, with a state for each port.

Picks the picture on a port's VMU screen for vmuScreenUpdate, unless the port has no screen ready: 0 the default picture, 1 the chain (vmuChainShow), 2 while a save writes, 3 while a load reads, 4 after a save or a load that worked and 5 after one that failed.
Returns the last frame of a model's motion: its frame count minus 1, as a float. The id gives the bank in the high half and the model in the low half.
Moves a motion's frame by a step, backwards with flag 2. Past the last frame (modelMotionFrames) or below 0, flag 1 wraps the frame around, else it stops at that end and the function returns 1.
Draws a model at a frame of a motion, with functions for each node (modelTreeDraw).

Walks a tree of node records for modelDrawNodes. For each node it applies the motion to the matrix (njMotionTransformEx), calls the node's callback with the caller's value and draws the node object's model with the node's draw function or the default one, unless the object's hidden flag (8) is set. Then it walks the node's child, and the node's siblings in turn.
Draws a model at a frame of a motion.
Draws a sprite as a quad in the current matrix.
The draw flags of an enemy's model: its color, and a flash in a frame in which it was hit.
Draws an enemy's model with enemyModelFlags.
Draws an enemy's model at a frame of its motion with enemyModelFlags.

Makes a bullet with a color, a position and a velocity, and with the first sprite and the angle that the caller gives. It keeps a pointer to a scale for each draw, none with 0, which every caller in the game passes. bulletSpriteUpdate and bulletSpriteDraw run it in list 4.
A sprite bullet's task: moves it as bulletUpdate does and animates it through 4 frames.
Draws a sprite bullet and files its hit record.
Makes a bullet with a fixed sprite that turns.
A turning bullet's task: moves it as bulletUpdate does and turns it at each frame.
Draws a turning bullet and files its hit record.

Turns on light 2 of the multi-light models as a point light with a position, a color and a range, and turns the lights into the view (lightsTurnApply). Flag 1 sets it for the Easy models and flag 2 for the Simple models.
Switches light 2 of the multi-light models off (lightOn's point light): flag 1 for the Easy models and flag 2 for the Simple models.

The task of a flash (effectFlash): while it has an owner task, it copies the followed position and ends when the owner's removal starts. It steps the animation, negates its x scale on random frames and ends at the animation's end.
Draws a flash (effectFlash) at its position, with the camera's depth taken from its z, and with its own depth value (spriteAtMatrixDepth).

Finds this game's places in the rankings of the difficulty, into rankPlaces, and returns 1 if a score has a place. With one player it ranks the player's total and chapter scores (lists 0 to 5), with two players their added scores (chapterScoresTotal, lists 6 to 11). With two players it does nothing during a name entry and, outside the ending, until both players are out.
Starts a player's name entry: sets its bit in nameEntryPlayers and makes the name entry's task (nameEntryTask) in list 5. playerOut calls it when a score has a place in the rankings.

The draw of the name entry's task (nameEntryStart): runs the input (nameEntryInput) and draws the entry (nameEntryDraw) for up to 1860 frames, then fills the rest of the name (nameEntryEnd). 90 frames after the name is complete it starts the player's continue (continueStart), except in the ending, and clears the player's bit in nameEntryPlayers.
Draws a player's name entry: the seconds left from 30, the score, place and list of each ranking where the game has a place (rankPlaces), and the name's three letters with the cursor.
Makes a player's HUD: a task in list 5.
The HUD's task: follows chainSet and keeps a complete set on the HUD for 62 frames.

Draws a player's HUD: the score, which in a game with two players changes with their total (scoreTotal), the lives, the chain display, and the energy as a number in the prototype mode, else as the gauge (energyGaugeBuild). For a ship out of the game it shows hudPressStart instead.

Sets the energy gauge's boxes, which hudDraw draws: a box for each 10 of playerEnergy, which is one homing laser at a release (playerButtons). Full boxes take the polarity's color and a part box pulses. It sets the boxes' places only when the energy changed or the game is paused.

Adds two scores, with the sum of their last digits held at 9 or less. A score's last digit starts as the player's continues (playerStart). hudDraw and chapterScoresTotal use it for a game with two players.

Blinks a text in the place of player 1 or 2 (0 or 1) who does not play: the game-over text when no credit is left or while the player's count at playerGameOverTimer runs down from 127, which the continue's end sets. Else a text to press Start, or a text to wait while a name entry runs or the player cannot join yet. With 2 it blinks a text to press Start in the middle, or in the tutorial outside the demo a text to skip, only in a trial. It draws nothing while the player continues or enters a name, while gameOver is set, or while sceneRequest is set.

Makes the effect at one side of a player's ship while a chapter's sequence flies the ships, a task of shipSideEffectUpdate and shipSideEffectDraw. The sequences of all five chapters make two for each player: flag bit 7 gives the player and flag bit 0 the side.

The task of the effect at one side of a player's ship (shipSideEffectCreate). It ends with its parent task, and in step 0 it makes particles from frame 121 and, on the side with flag bit 0 clear, plays sound 0x16 at frame 150. After its parent has moved it to step 2, it starts the player's vibration on that side, narrows and stretches its 3D sprites, waits, then shrinks, fades out and ends.

Draws the effect at one side of a player's ship (shipSideEffectCreate) in the ship's matrix, with sprite flags by the player's polarity. It draws three sprites, one of them turned by its direction from the screen's centre, and from step 3 on two crossed 3D sprites with an animated frame.

Places the 12 frames of the energy gauge by the screen's orientation, optionScreenX and optionScreenY, and sets the depth of the gauge's boxes. hudCreate calls it, and hudDraw calls it again while the game is paused.
Takes a credit for a join or a continue. Returns 0 when no credit is left, and 1 without taking one in free play (credits 0xFF).

At a join (playerJoinCheck) or a continue (continueTask), adds the player's continueNext to playerContinues, which stops at 255. continueStart sets continueNext to 1, so a join before the player's first continue does not count.

Starts the continue for a player: sets its bit in playersContinuing and its continueNext to 1. Outside the ending it sets continueTimer to 9 and makes the continue's task (continueTask, removed by continueEnd).

The draw of the continue's task (continueStart), which draws the continue with continueScreen. On Start with a credit the player joins again (playerJoin) with a continue counted (playerContinueAdd). When the count has run out the continue ends and gameOverCheck may start the game over.

Draws a player's continue text, which blinks and changes between the count of continueTimer and a second text that depends on the credits, or a wait text during a name entry. Returns 2 when the player presses Start and a credit is left (creditUse), 1 when the count has run out, else 0. A or B skips the rest of the current count.
The removal of the continue's task (continueStart). Unless continueTask ended the task itself, it clears the player's bit in playersOut and sets the player's byte of playerGameOverTimer to 0x7f.

Lets a player who is not in the game join with Start when a credit is left (creditUse): counts a continue (playerContinueAdd), calls playerJoin and in the prototype mode sets the energy to 500 - 200 * difficulty. It does nothing during a name entry or while the player's bit in playersOut or joinLocked is set. Returns 1 when the player joined.

Starts the game over when it does not run yet, no player is in the game, no ship is still dying on its last life and no player is at the name entry: makes the game over's task (gameOverTask), fades to black over 180 frames, stops all sounds and plays sound 0x3b. Returns 1 when the game over neither runs nor starts. continueTask calls it when a continue runs out.

The draw of the game over's task (gameOverCheck): draws two sprites that fade in, and after 180 frames removes the tasks up to level 200 in lists 0 to 6. 120 frames later, with the sprites faded out, it adds the play time (playTimeAdd) and changes to scene 3, the rankings with this game's play data (rankingAfterGame), or in the practice mode to the title (scene 4).

A player lost the last life: starts the name entry if a score has a place in the rankings (rankingFindPlaces), else the continue (continueStart). With gameNoRanking set it skips the rankings. It also stops the player from pausing (pauseLocked).

The draw function of the title's task, which has no update: runs the screen of titleState at each frame. See docs/game.md, The title and its menus. States 12 and 13 free its text lines and, after a wait, request the scene in byte 7 of its data.
The removal function of the title's task (sceneTitleStart sets it): frees the title's text lines (textLineFree).
Title state 0: waits for Start, and after 900 frames plays the attract demo, in turns the tutorial, chapter 1 and chapter 2.
Title state 1: GAME START, PRACTICE, RANKING, CONFIG, TUTORIAL, APPENDIX, BACKUP and EXIT.
Title state 2: CONTROLLER SETTING, each player's buttons and vibration.
Title state 3: the RANKING menu with VIEW RANKING, CLEAR RANKING and EXIT. VIEW RANKING requests scene 3 (sceneRankingStart) and CLEAR RANKING opens title state 4 (rankingResetScreen).
Title state 4: asks before rankingDefaults clears the rankings.
Title state 5: CONFIG, with MONITOR TYPE, SOUND, DIFFICULTY, TRIAL GAME, EXTEND, PLAYER STOCK, CONTROLLER SETTING, DEFAULT and EXIT.

Title state 6: PRACTICE, chapters 1 to 5 for each of the three difficulties. A chapter can be picked when chapterReached for its difficulty is at least its number, and its game then starts with credits 0xff and gamePractice set.
Title state 7: AUTO SAVE, LOAD, SAVE and EXIT, with the play time.
Title state 9: APPENDIX's four items, each shown after a condition, such as a trial cleared with one credit or 5 hours of play.

Title state 11: the APPENDIX's GALLERY 1, GALLERY 2 and SOUND TEST, by the item that appendixMenu picked. It loads the current entry's picture into bank 2, and left and right step through the entries. X turns the help on or off. In the SOUND TEST, A or C plays the entry's sequence and Y fades it out.

Unless the game is over, makes the results' task in list 0 (resultsUpdate, resultsDraw), which shows the boss destroy bonus, the chapter's score and max chain, and the play rank from the score table that it gets. It sets stageEvents flags 0x02 and 0x08, and outside scene 10 it sets forced flags 0x02 and 0x08 on both ships and clears their release.
The task of the results: runs their steps, five a frame while A or B is held.
Draws the two sprites 0x11b00 and 0x11b01 of the results at the alpha in its byte 2, which resultsStep fades in and out. The texts are tasks of their own (resultsTextCreate).

Runs one frame of the results by their step (byte 0): it waits, shows the boss destroy bonus and adds it to the scores (bossTimeLeft times 10000), stores the chapter scores and shows the chapter's score, max chain and play rank (resultsTextCreate, resultsPlayRank), then fades out. Returns 1 when it is done.
Clears bossTimeLeft, at each stageStart.
Adds a number of seconds to bossTimeLeft. bossTimerUpdate calls it with the seconds left plus 1 when the timer's end flag is set before its time runs out.

Makes a boss's timer, a task in list 4 (bossTimerUpdate, bossTimerDraw), from an owner task, the addresses of a start flag and an end flag, and a number of seconds. The timer counts the seconds down once the start flag is set and sets the end flag when they run out.

The task of a boss's timer: it moves into its place, waits for the start flag, then counts its seconds down once every 60 frames, copied to bossTimer, and sets the end flag when they run out. When the end flag is set first, it adds the seconds left plus 1 to bossTimeLeft (bossTimeAdd). It then blinks for 256 frames and ends, and it ends at once when its owner's task is marked for removal.
Draws a boss timer's text with its seconds, unless nameEntryPlayers has flag 0x02 or the game is over. After the timer stops, the text blinks, hidden 8 of every 32 frames.
The task of SELECT GAME MODE: with USER SELECT it asks for the difficulty, with TRIAL GAME on for the normal or the trial game, then requests chapter 1 or the tutorial.
Draws the mode select (modeSelectUpdate): its sprites, the choices, hudPressStart for a player who is not in the game, and the seconds left to choose.
Moves the mode select's choice with up and down.
Sets difficultyChoice and difficulty from the mode select's choice.
Makes the camera, a task in list 0 whose data sceneCamera points at.

The camera's task: places it on its orbit about its point (cameraOrbit), mixes that view with the one at target by blend when blend is above 0, turns the main light with its angles (lightAim) and builds its view matrix (cameraView).
Sets the perspective and the view for the draws.
Clears sceneCamera at the camera's removal.

The draw of the task in list 1 that cameraCreate makes: when the camera's mode is 1, sets the camera's flatPerspective and a unit matrix, turned by -0x4000 on a vertical screen, for the draws that follow.
Lowers the first byte of stageLocks by 1, so that stage command 3 (stageCmdNextPhase) can go on once it is 0. stageStart, resultsUpdate, bossDeathUpdate and other functions call it.
Makes a player's controller vibrate with a pattern for a time, while the player's vibration is on and no demo plays.
Finds the vibration unit in one of a controller's two sockets.
Returns 0, 1, 2 or 3 for the vibration unit at port 1, 2, 7 or 8 (vibrationPort), else -1.
Makes the task that starts a vibration. A newer request for the same unit makes the older task end without starting.
The task of a vibration: sets the unit's stop time and starts it.
Places the camera on its orbit about the point it follows.
Builds the camera's view matrix.
Turns the main light's direction with the view.
Gives the lights to Ninja's draws: the main light's direction and color and the ambient light.

Sets the light values to their defaults: the main light's two angles to 0, its color to 1, 1, 1 with intensity 1 and ambient 0.25, and three values for the multi-light models to 0.24. gameInit calls it.
